author: seia-soto
body:
fixes #5381

From the nytimes.com breakage https://github.com/ghostery/broken-page-reports/issues/2069, `:xpath` pseudo class selector is known for creating number of executions. Here, I found two improvements could be made: (a) reusing xpath expressions (b) incorrectly pushing all elements to the result candidates from `querySelectorAll` method.

## Delegation check

The second one: **delegation check for pseudo selector** includes logical changes and this requires a strict review. It might be seen as a temporal fix for the issue as the same issue may happen again with different selector. Also, it exposes the unoptimised code path from the whole evaluation process.

Looking at the `querySelectorAll` method, you can see it will run `element.querySelectorAll('*')` to load all elements into the candidates list. This creates a lot of duplicated query due to the nature of xpath evaluation which handles all the elements under the given `element`.

`isDelegatedPseudoClass` method create a way to check if the method is delegating the query into another method such as DOM query or xpath query. When the selector is marked as "delegated" by this method, it means the query will be outsourced and the delegating entity is responsible for searching all of the child nodes.

https://github.com/ghostery/adblocker/blob/master/packages/adblocker-extended-selectors/src/eval.ts#L463-L476

### Further directions

It seems like `:has` also can be extremely slow when the specific conditions are met.

## Measurement

The measurement were done manually but the actual behaviours are demonstrated as below.

### In case of `:xpath(query)`

1. `packages/adblocker-extended-selectors/src/eval.ts:querySelectorAll` is called with `document.documentElement` and `[PseudoClass{name: 'xpath'}]`.
2. From `if (selector.type === 'pseudo-class')`, `element.querySelectorAll('*')` is called and each element is passed to `traverse()` with the given selector.

In section 2, it shouldn't be querying more than one time since the evaluation of `xpath` on `document.documentElement` must include all the results coming from the view of its children. Especially here, it shouldn't query as many as the number of elements in the document.

- Updated `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` to run `make docs-clean` immediately after checkout so generated docs are cleaned before artifacts are downloaded.

author: kyrapieterse
body:
### Motivation
- Switching responsive breakpoints (notably XL → XXL) is slow because XXL CSS is regenerated per block on each switch.

### Description
- Add per-block XXL cache fields `xxlStyleCache` and `isXxlStyleCacheDirty` to `MaxiBlockComponent` to avoid unnecessary regeneration of XXL CSS.
- Thread a new `isBaseBreakpointChange` parameter through `displayStyles`, `injectStyles`, and `generateStyleContent` to make cache validity decisions aware of base breakpoint changes.
- Use the cached XXL CSS when switching to the `xxl` breakpoint if `xxlStyleCache` exists and `isXxlStyleCacheDirty` is `false`, and save the generated XXL CSS back to `xxlStyleCache` when computed.
- Mark the XXL cache dirty when style-impacting changes occur (non-relation attribute changes, `baseBreakpoint` changes, or `blockStyle` changes) so the cache is invalidated and recomputed when necessary.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change.
- Please run the repository's unit tests and style/test suites (for example `npm test`) after pulling to verify integration and performance improvements.

------

Expanded sshpiperd coverage and safety by adding focused unit tests and guards to validate chain plugin flow, auth method selection, and callback routing.

- **Metadata propagation in chaining**: Verifies `onNextPlugin` advances index and merges metadata when moving to the next plugin.
- **Auth method selection**: Ensures default auth methods are derived when callbacks exist, custom methods override when provided, and partial callback sets only advertise available methods.
- **Callback delegation and guards**: Confirms `InstallPiperConfig` routes per-plugin callbacks (none, password, publickey, keyboard-interactive, banner) based on the active plugin index, guards nil callbacks with consistent auth-terminology errors instead of panicking, and asserts error messages for guard and no-more-plugins paths.

Example snippet:

methods, _ := cp.NextAuthMethods(conn, &chainConnMeta{})

author: wisemrmusa
body:
This PR builds on `nm/01-guest-program` to add comprehensive automation scripts for generating fixtures, running gas-categorized benchmarks, and significantly improves the SP1 cluster setup with better error handling, configurability, and health checks.

---

## Detailed Changes

### 1. Benchmark Automation Scripts

#### `scripts/generate-gas-categorized-fixtures.sh`

Generates witness files organized by gas categories from EEST fixtures:

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Gas categories | Support for 1M, 10M, 30M, 45M, 60M, 100M, 150M and custom values |
| Rational numbers | Support formats like `0.5M`, `1.5M`, `2.5M` |
| Local EEST support | `--eest-fixtures-path` to use local fixtures |
| Dry run mode | `--dry-run` to preview commands |
| Parallel processing | Leverages Rayon with configurable thread count |

```bash
# Example usage
./scripts/generate-gas-categorized-fixtures.sh -g 1M,10M,30M
./scripts/generate-gas-categorized-fixtures.sh -e ./local-fixtures -g 0.5M,1M
```

#### `scripts/run-gas-categorized-benchmarks.sh`

Main script for executing benchmarks across gas categories:

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-z, --zkvm` | Select zkVM: risc0, sp1, openvm, pico, zisk, airbender |
| `-e, --execution-client` | Choose reth or ethrex |
| `-r, --resource` | Resource type: cpu, gpu, network, cluster |
| `-c, --gas-categories` | Gas categories to benchmark |
| `-a, --action` | prove or execute |
| `-g, --guest` | stateless-executor or stateless-validator |
| `-m, --memory-tracking` | Enable memory profiling |
| `-f, --force-rerun` | Bypass cached results |
| `-n, --dry-run` | Preview commands |

```bash
# Example usage
./scripts/run-gas-categorized-benchmarks.sh -z sp1 -c 1M,10M -r gpu
./scripts/run-gas-categorized-benchmarks.sh -z risc0 -a execute -g stateless-executor
```

### 2. Opcode Analysis Scripts

#### `scripts/trace_opcodes.py`

Comprehensive opcode tracing and analysis tool (~1169 lines):

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Opcode extraction | Extract opcodes from bytecode |
| Execution tracing | Trace opcode execution sequences |
| Gas analysis | Analyze gas consumption per opcode |
| Statistics | Generate instruction breakdown statistics |
| CSV export | Export results to CSV for analysis |

#### `scripts/analyze_opcode_traces.py`

Analyzes traced opcode execution data:

| Output | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Instruction counts | Per-opcode execution frequency |
| Gas breakdown | Gas consumption by opcode type |
| Hotspot detection | Identify expensive operations |

#### `scripts/trace-opcodes-by-gas-category.sh`

Wrapper script for tracing opcodes across gas categories.

### 3. SP1 Cluster Enhancements

Major improvements to `scripts/sp1-cluster/`:

#### `start-sp1-cluster.sh` Improvements

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Configurable resources** | All resource limits via environment variables |
| **NVIDIA detection** | Comprehensive GPU/runtime verification with installation guides |
| **Docker Compose v1/v2** | Support for both legacy and modern Docker Compose |

Added `--risc0-keccak-limit` option for controlling keccak cycle limits:

```bash
./ere-hosts prove --zkvm risc0 --risc0-keccak-limit 1000000
```

- Clearer resource type descriptions
- Network/cluster validation for SP1
- Better error messages

### Automation Benefits

1. **Reproducibility**: Standardized scripts ensure consistent benchmark runs
2. **Flexibility**: Support for multiple gas categories, zkVMs, and configurations

4. **Efficiency**: Dry-run modes prevent wasted compute time

### SP1 Cluster Benefits

## Description

The management plane generator incorrectly named flattened properties when the inner property name was a plural form of a word in the parent property name after suffix stripping. For example, `ApplicationProfile.galleryApplications` would generate `ApplicationGalleryApplications` instead of `GalleryApplications`.

### Changes

**Generator Logic (`PropertyHelpers.GetCombinedPropertyName`)**
- Track when suffixes (Profile, Policy, Configuration, Properties, Settings) are stripped from parent property names
- Check both pluralized and singularized forms of the inner property's last word against parent words
- Apply singularize check only when a suffix was stripped to prevent false matches with natural property name components

**Test Coverage**

author: scrrlt
body:
## Summary
- declare every backend dependency in `pyproject.toml`, cap Python to <3.14,
  disable Poetry’s package mode so installs succeed, and add a `dev` extra
  (`pytest>=8.3,<9.0`) — then regenerate `poetry.lock` and align
  `requirements.txt` to match those ranges
- remove RagAnything from the default dependency list, introduce a shared
  `src/knowledge/raganything_loader.py`, and refactor the ingestion scripts
  plus `rag_tool.py` to log a clear warning and skip MinerU-backed flows when
  the optional dependency is missing instead of crashing the entire app
- document the new workflow in `README.md`, explicitly outlining the dependency
  layers (core backend via `poetry install --no-root`, dev extras via
  `--extras dev`, optional RagAnything/MinerU install, and frontend npm setup),
  and update `tests/core/test_prompt_manager.py` so caching behavior remains
  testable without RagAnything on the path

## Root Cause
Fresh environments that skipped RagAnything (and therefore MinerU) hit a
`ModuleNotFoundError` during import because our ingestion modules pulled
RagAnything at module load. Once that happened FastAPI never even started,
rendering the whole application unusable for those that only needed the core
features.

## Fix
Treat RagAnything as an optional capability at the application boundary:
imports are now wrapped, missing dependencies emit human-friendly logs, and
the rest of the system stays operational. Advanced PDF/OCR ingestion still
requires installing RagAnything + MinerU manually, and the README now calls
that out. Fully decoupling MinerU inside RagAnything would still require
upstream changes (feature flags, guarded imports, fallback parsers), but this
PR ensures the host app degrades gracefully in the meantime.

## Dependency Model (for reviewers)
- **Core backend** – `poetry install --no-root`, using the ranges declared in
  `pyproject.toml`.
- **Developer extras** – `poetry install --no-root --extras dev`, which brings
  in pytest and the rest of the test/lint tooling.
- **RagAnything/MinerU (optional)** – Not installed by default. Teams wanting
  PDF/OCR ingestion should install RagAnything alongside this repo and follow
  its instructions for MinerU.
- **Frontend** – `npm install --prefix web` remains unchanged.

## Testing
- py -3.13 -m poetry run ruff check src/knowledge/add_documents.py src/knowledge/initializer.py src/tools/rag_tool.py
- py -3.13 -m poetry run pytest tests/core/test_prompt_manager.py

## Notes
`src/knowledge/raganything_loader.py` now bundles the lazy import logic for the
ingestion scripts and RAG tool. If we later fork RagAnything to make MinerU
optional upstream, we can swap out the helper’s internals in one place without
touching the rest of the application.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent UI refresh bugs and noisy AbortError logs by introducing a safe, reusable fetch pattern.  
- Give users a fast, non-blocking way to find orders, delivered history and clients from the top bar.  
- Provide a compact 30-day summary card on the dashboard with key averages and top lists to improve quick decision making.  

### Description
- Add a reusable hook `useSafeQuery` implementing abort-safety, deduping in-flight requests, and auto-refresh on window `focus` and `online` events with a small minimal API (`key`, `fetcher`, `deps`, `options`).  
- Replace manual abort logic in `History` with `useSafeQuery` and wire reading `search` query param so history reloads reliably without manual refresh.  
- Make `loadDashboardMetrics` accept an optional `AbortSignal` and call it through `useSafeQuery` from `App` so dashboard metrics auto-refresh safely.  
- Add `GlobalSearch` component (debounced 300ms) in the top bar with grouped, limited results for `orders`, `history`/delivered, and `clients`, using `useSafeQuery` for abort safety.  
- Add a compact `DailySummaryCard` to the dashboard that computes averages for `cut-and-bend` and `straight-bar` (last 30 days), top 3 diameters and top 3 clients, and fetches only the required columns.  

### Testing
- Started the dev server with `npm run dev` which reported Vite ready and served at `http://localhost:4173/` (succeeded).  
- Ran a Playwright script to open `http://127.0.0.1:4173/` and capture a screenshot (`artifacts/dashboard.png`), which completed and produced the artifact (succeeded).  
- No automated unit test suite was added or run as part of this change.  
- Manual runtime checks verified that dashboard metrics and history use the safe fetch pattern and that aborts are ignored rather than logged as database errors.

author: ximon18
body:
The intent of this PR was to generate a modified Cascade config that the user could inspect and use, in the cases where changes to their config are required, e.g. to configure Cascade to publish signed zones on the same interfaces as the given OpenDNSSEC configuration uses.

However this PR is incomplete and on-hold because Cascade doesn't currently support serializing its `Config` or `Spec` types, only deserialization is supported.

This is not a huge problem as `main` already prints instructions to the user on how to modify their Cascade config, it would just be more user friendly and less error prone to generate proposed config changes for the user instead of them having to do it manually themselves.

author: copilot
body:
AWS Transcribe's unreliable language detection (`detected_language` returns `en-US` for Chinese text) prevented translation. The Cantonese-biased configuration blocked proper Mandarin support.

## Changes

**Endpoint Implementation**
- Replaced AWS Transcribe WebSocket proxy with delegation to existing `transcribe_alibaba`
- Removed 307 lines: event stream encoding/parsing, presigned URL generation, AWS signature logic

**Language Detection**
- Switched from ASR labels to CJK character detection (`\u4e00-\u9fff`)
- Cantonese vs Mandarin determined by characteristic characters (`嘅咩喺咗冇哋啲呢啦噉仲咪睇醫`)
- Configured with `language_hints=["en", "yue", "zh"]`

**Default Configuration**
- Enabled `ENABLE_ALIBABA_TRANSLATION=1` and `ENABLE_ALIBABA_ENTITIES=1` by default

## Breaking Changes

The `language_code` query parameter is no longer accepted. Language detection is automatic.

## Before/After

**Before:**
```python
# 159 lines of AWS proxy logic + event stream encoding/decoding
async with session.ws_connect(aws_url) as aws_ws:
    # Complex bidirectional forwarding
    # Translation only if detected_language != "en-US" (often wrong)
```

**After:**
```python
@app.websocket("/client-transcribe")
async def client_transcribe(ws: WebSocket):
    await transcribe_alibaba(ws)  # Uses CJK detection
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> The current transcription implementation in `main.py` uses AWS Transcribe with a configuration that biases towards Cantonese (`zh-HK`) and fails to translate Chinese text because it relies on AWS's often incorrect `detected_language` label (returning `en-US` for Chinese).
> 
> This PR switches the `/client-transcribe` endpoint in `main.py` to use the Alibaba Paraformer implementation (`api.v1.transcribe.transcribe_alibaba`). 
> 
> Specific improvements:
> 1.  **Translation Fix**: Uses content-based detection (checking for CJK characters) instead of unreliable ASR language labels to trigger translation.
> 2.  **Language Support**: Configures Alibaba Paraformer with `["en", "yue", "zh"]` hints, enabling correct support for Mandarin, Cantonese, and English.
> 3.  **Cleanup**: Removes legacy AWS Transcribe proxy code, event stream parsers, and associated imports from `main.py`.
> 4.  **Defaults**: Updates `api/v1/transcribe.py` to enable translation and entity detection by default (`ENABLE_ALIBABA_TRANSLATION=1`).
> 
> This resolves the issues where Chinese text was not being translated and transcription was locked to Cantonese.

author: copilot
body:
Ports the MuQSS (Multiple Queue Skiplist Scheduler) v0.210 from kernel 5.13 to 5.19.17.

## Changes

**New scheduler implementation:**
- `kernel/sched/MuQSS.c` (8.3K lines): Core MuQSS scheduler
- `kernel/skip_list.c`: Skip list data structure for runqueue management
- `kernel/Kconfig.MuQSS`: Runqueue sharing configuration (SMT/MC/SMP/none)

**Build system:**
- `kernel/sched/Makefile`: Added conditional compilation for MuQSS vs CFS
  - MuQSS path: builds MuQSS.o + minimal core (clock, cputime, idle, wait, completion)
  - CFS path: builds standard scheduler (core, fair, rt, deadline, loadavg, cpupri, pelt)
- `init/Kconfig`: CONFIG_SCHED_MUQSS option (default=y)

**Scheduler integration:**
- `include/linux/sched.h`: Task structure extended for MuQSS runqueue tracking
- `kernel/sysctl.c`: Added iso_cpu, rr_interval, interactive sysctl knobs
- Architecture configs: Updated x86, ARM, ARM64, PowerPC, Alpha for MuQSS support

**Driver compatibility:**
- Updated ~70 drivers using schedule_timeout(1) → schedule_min_hrtimeout()
- Timer subsystem changes for MuQSS's high-resolution requirements

## Notes

- Original Makefile was incomplete (34 lines, missing standard build rules); manually reconstructed the conditional build logic based on patch intent
- MuQSS replaces SCHED_DEADLINE with SCHED_ISO (UAPI change)
- Thermal pressure accounting disabled under MuQSS
- Patch applied with offsets due to kernel evolution (5.13 → 5.19.17) but no functional conflicts

body: ## #️⃣ 연관된 이슈 > #MOPL-70 ## #️⃣ 작업 내용 이번 PR은 **콘텐츠 삭제(Delete) API 구현**과 함께, 콘텐츠 도메인에 **논리 삭제(Soft Delete) 정책을 도입**하고 이에 따른 **도메인 / 서비스 / API / JPA / 테스트 전반 보완**을 포함합니다. 삭제 요청 시 실제 데이터를 제거하지 않고 `deletedAt`을 설정하여 향후 복구 가능성과 정책 확장 여지를 남기는 방향으로 설계했습니다. ### **API 추가** * `DELETE /api/contents/{contentId}` 엔드포인트 추가 * `ContentController`에 삭제 API 구현 * `ContentApiSpec`에 삭제 스펙 정의 * `ContentControllerTest`에 삭제 시나리오 테스트 추가 ### **도메인 모델 변경** * `ContentModel`에 `deleteContent()` 메서드 추가 * `deletedAt` 기반 Soft Delete 수행 * 이미 삭제된 경우 상태를 유지하는 **멱등성 보장** * 삭제 행위를 도메인 수준의 명확한 행위로 표현 * `ContentModelTest`에 삭제 및 멱등성 테스트 추가 ### **Service 계층 삭제 로직 구현** * `ContentService.delete()` 메서드 추가 * 콘텐츠 조회 → 도메인 삭제 → 저장 흐름으로 처리 * 삭제 요청이 여러 번 들어와도 동일하게 동작하도록 설계 * 연관 관계(ContentTag 등)는 즉시 제거하지 않고 별도 정책에 위임 * `ContentServiceTest`에 삭제 관련 테스트 보완 ### **JPA 엔티티 Soft Delete 적용** * `ContentEntity`에 `@SQLRestriction("deleted_at IS NULL")` 적용 * 삭제된 콘텐츠가 기본 조회에서 자동으로 제외되도록 처리 * 팀 내 `UserEntity` Soft Delete 패턴과 구조를 맞춤 * `ContentEntityTest` 신규 작성 * 저장/수정 시 auditing 필드 검증 * `deletedAt` 설정 시 조회 제외 동작 검증 ### **Facade 계층 연동** * `ContentFacade.delete()` 추가 * 트랜잭션 경계 내에서 서비스 삭제 로직 위임 * `ContentFacadeTest`에 삭제 흐름 테스트 추가 ## #️⃣ 테스트 결과 > ## #️⃣ 변경 사항 체크리스트 - [x] 코드에 영향이 있는 모든 부분에 대한 테스트를 작성하고 실행했나요? - [x] 코드 컨벤션에 따라 코드를 작성했나요? - [x] 본 PR에서 발생할 수 있는 의존성 문제를 확인했나요? ## #️⃣ 스크린샷 > ## 💡 기술적 의사결정: 콘텐츠 삭제 정책 ### 1. 콘텐츠 Soft Delete 도입 * 콘텐츠는 리뷰, 태그, 플레이리스트 등 다양한 도메인과 연관됨 * 즉시 Hard Delete 시 복구가 불가능하고 연관 데이터 관리 부담이 큼 * `deletedAt` 기반 Soft Delete로 **이력 보존과 정책 확장성**을 우선 확보 ### 2. 리뷰(Review) Soft Delete를 즉시 적용하지 않은 이유 * 콘텐츠 하나에 수천 ~ 많게는 수만 개의 리뷰가 달릴 수 있음 * 콘텐츠 삭제 시 모든 리뷰를 함께 논리 삭제할 경우: * 대량 업데이트로 인한 성능 부담 * 트랜잭션 크기 증가 및 잠재적 락 이슈 우려 * 따라서 **현 시점에서는 콘텐츠만 Soft Delete 처리** * 리뷰 삭제는 추후: * 배치 처리 * purge 정책 * 혹은 조회 단계에서 콘텐츠 삭제 여부로 필터링 등의 방식으로 확장 가능하도록 열어둠 ### 3. 도메인 중심 설계 * 삭제를 단순 상태 변경이 아닌 `deleteContent()`라는 **명시적 도메인 행위**로 표현 * 멱등성을 도메인에서 보장하여 서비스/컨트롤러 단의 방어 코드 최소화 ### 4. 조회 정책 단순화 * `@SQLRestriction`을 통해 삭제된 데이터가 자동으로 조회에서 제외됨 * 애플리케이션 레벨에서 조건 분기 없이 일관된 조회 정책 유지 ## #️⃣ 리뷰 요청 사항 > **콘텐츠만 Soft Delete 처리한 결정**이 현재 단계에서 적절한지

body:
Automated: Migrate {target_path} from gsutil to gcloud storage

This CL is part of the on going effort to migrate from the legacy `gsutil` tool to the new and improved `gcloud storage` command-line interface.
`gcloud storage` is the recommended and modern tool for interacting with Google Cloud Storage, offering better performance, unified authentication, and a more consistent command structure with other `gcloud` components. 🚀

### Automation Details

This change was **generated automatically** by an agent that targets users of `gsutil`.
The transformations applied are based on the  [gsutil to gcloud storage migration guide](http://go/gsutil-gcloud-storage-migration-guide).

### ⚠️ Action Required: Please Review and Test Carefully

While we have based the automation on the migration guide, every use case is unique.
**It is crucial that you thoroughly test these changes in environments appropriate to your use-case before merging.**  
Be aware of potential differences between `gsutil` and `gcloud storage` that could impact your workflows.  
For instance, the structure of command output may have changed, requiring updates to any scripts that parse it. Similarly, command behavior can differ subtly; the `gcloud storage rsync` command has a different file deletion logic than `gsutil rsync`, which could lead to unintended file deletions.  

Our migration guides can help guide you through a list of mappings and some notable differences between the two tools.

Standard presubmit tests are run as part of this CL's workflow. **If you need to target an additional test workflow or require assistance with testing, please let us know.**

Please verify that all your Cloud Storage operations continue to work as expected to avoid any potential disruptions in production.

### Support and Collaboration

The `GCS CLI` team is here to help! If you encounter any issues, have a complex use case that this automated change doesn't cover, or face any other blockers, please don't hesitate to reach out.
We are happy to work with you to test and adjust these changes as needed.

**Contact:** `gcs-cli-hyd@google.com`

We appreciate your partnership in this important migration effort!

author: mpython77
body:
ISSUE 1: DELETED POSTS STILL BEING SENT
========================================
Problem:
- User schedules a post
- User deletes the post from UI
- Post is removed from database
- BUT scheduler still sends it!

Root Cause:
- Scheduler runs in a loop with in-memory list of posts
- When post is deleted, database is updated but scheduler already has the old list
- Scheduler doesn't re-check if post exists before sending

Solution:
- Added database check at start of send_scheduled_post()
- Verifies post still exists in database before sending
- Checks post status is still 'Pending'
- Skips sending if post was deleted or status changed
- Added get_scheduled_post_by_id() method to database.py

Changes in app.py:
- send_scheduled_post(): Added verification check
- If post deleted: "⚠️  Post ID X was deleted - skipping send"
- If status changed: "⚠️  Post ID X status is 'Y' - skipping send"

Changes in database.py:
- Added get_scheduled_post_by_id(post_id) method
- Returns post dict or None if not found

ISSUE 2: TIMEZONE MISMATCH (2-3 HOUR DIFFERENCE)
=================================================
Problem:
- User enters time: 19:00 (meaning 19:00 Tashkent time, UTC+5)
- System saves it as: 19:00 UTC+2
- Actual execution time: 22:00 Tashkent time (3 hour difference!)

Root Cause:
- Code hardcoded UTC+2 timezone: timezone(timedelta(hours=2))
- User's browser sends naive datetime (no timezone)
- Backend added UTC+2 timezone info, but user is in UTC+5 (Uzbekistan)
- Result: 3 hour difference between intended and actual time

Solution:
- REMOVED all timezone conversions
- Use naive datetimes (no timezone info) throughout
- Treat all times as server's local time
- User enters time → saves as-is → executes at that time

Changes in app.py:
1. add_scheduled_posts():
   - Changed: current_time = datetime.now() (was datetime.now(utc_plus_1))
   - Changed: slot_datetime parsing - NO timezone added
   - Removed: .replace(tzinfo=utc_plus_1)

2. run_scheduler():
   - Changed: current_time = datetime.now() (was datetime.now(utc_plus_1))
   - Changed: post_time parsing - NO timezone added
   - Added: Remove timezone if present: post_time.replace(tzinfo=None)
   - All datetime comparisons now naive vs naive

Benefits:
- Time entered = time executed
- No confusing timezone conversions
- Works correctly regardless of server location
- Predictable behavior for users

Testing:
- Delete a scheduled post → verify it doesn't send
- Schedule post for "19:00" → verify it sends at 19:00 server time
- No more 2-3 hour time differences

Release notes
Package name: react
  • 19.2.3 - 2025-12-11

    React Server Components

    • Add extra loop protection to React Server Functions (@ sebmarkbage #35351)
  • 19.2.2 - 2025-12-11

    React Server Components

    • Move react-server-dom-webpack/*.unbundled to private react-server-dom-unbundled (@ eps1lon #35290)
    • Patch Promise cycles and toString on Server Functions (@ sebmarkbage, @ unstubbable #35289, #35345)
  • 19.2.1 - 2025-12-03

    React Server Components

    • Bring React Server Component fixes to Server Actions (@ sebmarkbage #35277)
  • 19.2.0 - 2025-10-01

    Below is a list of all new features, APIs, and bug fixes.

    Read the React 19.2 release post for more information.

    New React Features

    • <Activity>: A new API to hide and restore the UI and internal state of its children.
    • useEffectEvent is a React Hook that lets you extract non-reactive logic into an Effect Event.
    • cacheSignal (for RSCs) lets your know when the cache() lifetime is over.
    • React Performance tracks appear on the Performance panel’s timeline in your browser developer tools

    New React DOM Features

    • Added resume APIs for partial pre-rendering with Web Streams:
      • resume: to resume a prerender to a stream.
      • resumeAndPrerender: to resume a prerender to HTML.
    • Added resume APIs for partial pre-rendering with Node Streams:
      • resumeToPipeableStream: to resume a prerender to a stream.
      • resumeAndPrerenderToNodeStream: to resume a prerender to HTML.
    • Updated prerender APIs to return a postponed state that can be passed to the resume APIs.

    Notable changes

    • React DOM now batches suspense boundary reveals, matching the behavior of client side rendering. This change is especially noticeable when animating the reveal of Suspense boundaries e.g. with the upcoming <ViewTransition> Component. React will batch as much reveals as possible before the first paint while trying to hit popular first-contentful paint metrics.
    • Add Node Web Streams (prerender, renderToReadableStream) to server-side-rendering APIs for Node.js
    • Use underscore instead of : IDs generated by useId

    All Changes

    React

    • <Activity /> was developed over many years, starting before ClassComponent.setState (@ acdlite @ sebmarkbage and many others)
    • Stringify context as "SomeContext" instead of "SomeContext.Provider" (@ kassens #33507)

author: anneschuth
body:
## Summary

- Add platform-specific message size limits via `getMessageLimits()` interface
  - Slack: 12K max, 10K threshold (stricter due to markdown block limits at ~13K)
  - Mattermost: 16K max, 14K threshold (unchanged)
- Add error recovery when `updatePost` fails - automatically create new message instead of silently losing content
- Reset `currentPostId` on user follow-up messages so Claude's responses start in fresh messages
- Flush pending content before reset to properly close code blocks and other structures

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for error recovery (4 new tests in streaming.test.ts)
- [x] Unit tests for platform-specific limits (3 new tests in streaming.test.ts)
- [x] Unit tests for sendFollowUp flush/reset (5 new tests in lifecycle.test.ts)
- [ ] Manual test: Long Claude response in Slack doesn't silently fail
- [ ] Manual test: User follow-up creates new response message

body:
## Summary

This PR implements the `CacheStrategy` system as requested in #6, giving developers fine-grained control over how data is retrieved from cache vs remote source.

### Changes

- Added `CacheStrategy` enum with two strategies:
  - `cacheFirst` (default): Uses cache if available and valid, otherwise fetches from network
  - `networkFirst`: Always tries network first, falls back to cache (even expired) on failure
- Added `strategy` parameter to `call()` method
- Implemented fallback mechanism for `networkFirst` that uses expired cache data when network fails
- Added comprehensive test coverage (8 new tests)
- Updated README with usage examples, API reference, and FAQ

### Usage Example

```dart
// Network-first for fresh data with offline fallback
final news = await RemoteCaching.instance.call<News>(
  'latest_news',
  strategy: CacheStrategy.networkFirst,
  remote: () async => await newsService.getLatest(),
  fromJson: (json) => News.fromJson(json as Map<String, dynamic>),
);
```

### Backward Compatibility

- Default strategy remains `cacheFirst`, preserving existing behavior
- No breaking changes

## Test plan

- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] New tests for `cacheFirst` strategy behavior
- [x] New tests for `networkFirst` strategy behavior
- [x] Tests for network failure fallback to cache
- [x] Tests for expired cache fallback
- [x] Flutter analyze passes with no issues

Closes #6

## What does this PR do?
Microsoft.FileShares is the Azure Resource Provider for managing Azure File Shares and related operations such as snapshots, limits, and provisioning recommendations. This MCP integration exposes CLI commands aligned with the REST API operations defined in the Swagger specification.

This PR adds comprehensive support for the Microsoft.FileShares resource provider to Azure MCP Server, enabling AI agents to manage Azure File Shares, snapshots, and private endpoint connections through 15 commands across four operational categories.


## Changes

### New Toolset: Azure.Mcp.Tools.FileShares

Implemented a complete MCP toolset with **15 commands** across four categories:

#### 📁 File Share Management (5 commands)
- `azmcp fileshares fileshare get` - Get file share details
- `azmcp fileshares fileshare create` - Create new file share
- `azmcp fileshares fileshare update` - Update file share properties
- `azmcp fileshares fileshare delete` - Delete file share ⚠️ destructive
- `azmcp fileshares fileshare checknameavailability` - Validate name availability

#### 📸 Snapshot Operations (4 commands)
- `azmcp fileshares snapshot get` - Get snapshot details
- `azmcp fileshares snapshot create` - Create file share snapshot
- `azmcp fileshares snapshot update` - Update snapshot properties
- `azmcp fileshares snapshot delete` - Delete snapshot ⚠️ destructive

#### 📊 Informational Commands (3 commands)
- `azmcp fileshares fileshare getlimits` - Get regional limits and quotas
- `azmcp fileshares fileshare getprovisioningrecommendation` - Get provisioning recommendations
- `azmcp fileshares fileshare getusagedata` - Retrieve usage metrics and analytics

### Architecture & Implementation

- **Service Pattern**: `IFileSharesService` interface with `FileSharesService` implementation using Azure.ResourceManager APIs
- **Command Structure**: Follows established patterns with `BaseFileSharesCommand<T>` base class
- **Options Classes**: 15 strongly-typed options classes with proper validation
- **AOT Compatibility**: Full JSON serialization context registration for native compilation
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive exception handling with contextual error messages
- **Testing**: Complete unit test coverage + live test infrastructure (Bicep templates)

## Additional Context

This implementation follows the patterns established in KeyVault and Storage toolsets and adheres to all standards outlined in [new-command.md](../../servers/Azure.Mcp.Server/docs/new-command.md):

✅ Uses primary constructors for dependency injection

author: illidus
body:
### Motivation
- Make the odds-archive pipeline more accurate and auditable by preserving how URLs were discovered (sitemap/index/manual).
- Improve failure visibility when fetching pages by capturing HTTP status codes for errored fetches.
- Prevent ingestion of duplicate raw parser outputs by checking stable record hashes before appending.
- Provide a cohesive package of discovery/fetch/parse/normalize utilities to support repeatable archival runs.

### Description
- Added pipeline scripts `pipelines/odds_archive/01_discover_urls.py`, `02_fetch_extract_text.py`, `03_parse_props.py`, and `04_normalize_dedupe_export.py` to run discovery, fetch/extract, parsing, and normalization/export steps.
- Introduced `src/odds_archive` package including `config`, `discovery`, `fetch_extract`, `parsers`, `normalize`, `dedupe`, `schema`, and `utils`, and updated `io` with `load_jsonl_hashes` for reading existing `record_hash` values.
- Discovery now runs sitemaps, index pages, and manual URLs separately and records the `discovery_method` for each URL, and fetch step catches `requests.HTTPError` to record `http_status` in the URL lake.
- Parser stage loads existing `record_hash` values and skips appending any raw candidate whose hash already exists, and normalization/dedupe/export builds the final deduplicated parquet and optional DuckDB tables.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change.

This PR updates the CardDemo application to support 17-digit card numbers instead of the previous 16-digit limit. Changes span across 35 files including COBOL copybooks, programs, BMS screen definitions, and JCL batch job definitions.

Key changes:
- **Copybooks (cpy)**: Updated PIC clauses from X(16)/9(16) to X(17)/9(17) for card number fields, with corresponding FILLER adjustments to maintain record lengths
- **COBOL programs (cbl)**: Updated file descriptors and working storage fields, adjusted FILLER fields to preserve record sizes
- **BMS maps**: Changed LENGTH=16 to LENGTH=17 for card number input/output fields, adjusted screen positions
- **BMS copybooks (cpy-bms)**: Updated CARDSIDI/CARDSIDO and CARDNUMI/CARDNUMO fields
- **JCL files**: Updated KEYS specifications for VSAM file definitions and SORT field positions

### Motivation
- Prevent empty target columns by verifying price data contains usable close values before target generation.
- Attempt an automated refresh of price history when the database cache is empty or contains invalid close values so downstream target computation has a chance to succeed.
- Increase available historical training data by extending the default lookback window from 5 to 10 years.
- Improve dataset-build robustness and surface clear warnings when tickers must be skipped due to missing close values.

### Description
- Change the default `PredictorConfig.start_date` in `stock_predictor/core/config.py` from `date.today() - timedelta(days=365 * 5)` to `date.today() - timedelta(days=365 * 10)` to expand the lookback window.
- Add `_has_usable_close` helper and integrate it into `MultiHorizonModelingEngine.build_dataset` in `stock_predictor/core/modeling/multi_horizon_engine.py` to detect when price frames lack usable close values.
- When `get_prices` returns empty or invalid frames, attempt a forced refresh via `fetcher.fetch_price_data(force=True)` and log a `price_refresh` stage if refreshed data is available.
- If a ticker still lacks usable close values after refresh, skip it with a warning to avoid producing empty target columns; other sample-selection and target-generation logic is unchanged.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this rollout.
- Unit tests and CI were not run for these changes.
- No automated test failures were reported because no tests were run.

**Summary**

This PR fixes **GitHub issue #548** by ensuring Nostr dispute events explicitly include who initiated the dispute (buyer or seller).

**Details**

- Add an `initiator` custom tag to NIP-33 dispute events with value `"buyer"` or `"seller"`.

Having the dispute initiator in the event metadata makes it easier for clients and tooling to reason about disputes, improves auditability, and directly addresses the requirements described in **issue #548**.

## Summary
# Change Summary
- Added `%` operator support in the calculator core and CLI argument choices/types.
- Added unit and end-to-end coverage for modulo behavior.
- Documented a modulo usage example in the README.

# Tests
- Not run (per instructions).

## Plan
# Implementation Plan: Support Modulo Operator

## Goal
Add support for the modulo (`%`) operator to the CLI calculator and its underlying calculation logic, ensuring unit and end-to-end tests cover the new behavior.

## Scope and Assumptions
- The calculator currently supports `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` and exposes a `calc <left> <operator> <right>` CLI command.
- Modulo behavior follows JavaScript’s remainder operator semantics (`a % b`).
- No new external libraries or APIs are required.

## Relevant Files (Reviewed)
- `src/cli.ts`: Defines `Operator` type and `calculate` implementation.
- `src/index.ts`: CLI definition, operator choices, and argument parsing.
- `tests/unit.test.ts`: Unit tests for `calculate`.
- `tests/e2e.test.ts`: CLI integration tests.
- `README.md`: Basic usage documentation.

## Plan

### 1) Extend core operator type and calculation logic
- Update `Operator` in `src/cli.ts` to include `%`.
- Extend the `calculate` switch statement with a `%` case that returns `left % right`.
- Ensure TypeScript remains exhaustive; if needed, add a default unreachable branch or rely on union narrowing.

### 2) Update CLI operator choices and typing
- In `src/index.ts`, add `%` to the `choices` array for the `operator` positional argument.
- Update the local `operator` type annotation to include `%` so the CLI invocation compiles and is type-safe.

### 3) Add unit test coverage for modulo
- In `tests/unit.test.ts`, add a new test case (e.g., `calculate(10, "%", 3)` yields `1`).
- Consider adding a second case that validates negative or fractional behavior only if the project conventions expect it (otherwise keep a single canonical test).

### 4) Add CLI end-to-end coverage for modulo
- In `tests/e2e.test.ts`, add a test that runs `calc 10 % 3` and asserts output `1`, empty stderr, and exit code `0`.

### 5) Documentation update (optional but recommended)
- In `README.md`, add an example that demonstrates modulo usage (e.g., `bun run src/index.ts calc 10 % 3`).

## Validation Checklist
- `bun test` passes all unit and e2e tests.
- `bun run src/index.ts calc 10 % 3` prints `1`.

## Notes
- No external libraries or API changes are needed for this request.

body:
## Summary

Implements Gmail sent email tracking as part of Phase 3 data fetchers.

This PR adds the Gmail fetcher which tracks sent emails from Gmail accounts and creates time entries for communication activities.

## Changes

### Core Implementation
- ✅ Gmail API wrapper (`GmailAPI` class)
- ✅ Gmail fetcher service (`GmailFetcher` class)  
- ✅ OAuth 2.0 authentication integration
- ✅ Sent email filtering by monitored recipients
- ✅ Email metadata extraction (subject, recipients)
- ✅ Configurable default duration (30 minutes)
- ✅ Raw event storage in PocketBase

### Testing
- ✅ 27 comprehensive unit tests
- ✅ API wrapper tests
- ✅ Fetcher logic tests
- ✅ OAuth integration tests
- ✅ Error handling tests
- ✅ All tests passing

### Configuration
New PocketBase settings (already in seed script):
- `gmail_enabled` - Enable/disable Gmail tracking
- `gmail_monitored_recipients` - Filter emails by recipient
- `gmail_default_duration_minutes` - Default time per email (30 min)

## Features

### Email Tracking
- Fetches sent emails from Gmail API
- Filters by configurable recipient list (optional)
- Extracts subject and recipients
- Default 30-minute duration per email
- Deduplication (skips existing events)

### Output Format
```
Description: "Email to client@example.com: Project Update"
Duration: 30 minutes (configurable)
Priority: 60 (medium-high)
Source: gmail
```

### OAuth Integration
- Secure token storage with encryption
- Automatic token refresh
- Multi-account support via PocketBase `email_accounts` collection

## Testing

All tests pass:
```bash
pytest tests/test_gmail_fetcher.py -v
# ======================= 27 passed, 15 warnings in 0.14s ========================
```

Test coverage includes:
- Gmail API integration
- Email filtering logic
- Configuration validation
- Error handling scenarios
- OAuth token management

## Dependencies

This PR depends on:
- ✅ Phase 2: Core Infrastructure (#2) - **Merged**
- ✅ Base fetcher class
- ✅ OAuth utilities
- ✅ PocketBase client

## Next Steps

After this PR:
1. Issue #6: GitHub Fetcher (Priority 4)
2. Issue #7: Cloud Events Fetcher (Priority 5)
3. Phase 4: Time Block Processor

## Usage

```python
from app.services.fetchers import GmailFetcher
from app.pocketbase_client import PocketBaseClient

# Initialize
pb_client = PocketBaseClient()
fetcher = GmailFetcher(
    pb_client=pb_client,
    account_email="user@gmail.com",
    credentials=oauth_credentials
)

# Fetch emails
result = fetcher.fetch()
print(f"Fetched {result.events_fetched} emails, created {result.events_created} events")
```

- [x] Settings schema configured
- [x] Documentation in docstrings
- [x] Follows project patterns (BaseFetcher)
- [x] OAuth integration working
- [x] Error handling implemented

author: zhiyuantang17
body:
## Introduction
This PR introduces the Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) for Realtek's **Bee Series SoCs**, specifically adding support for the **RTL87x2G** and **RTL8752H** series.

Realtek's [Bee Series SoCs](https://www.realmcu.com/en/Home/ProductOverview/BLE-2-4GHz-Zigbee-Thread-Matter) are multi-protocol wireless solutions (BLE, Zigbee, Thread, Matter) known for their excellent RF performance and ultra-low power consumption.

- **RTL87x2G Series**: High-performance multi-protocol SoCs. [Product Page](https://www.realmcu.com/en/Home/Products/RTL8762G-RTL877xG-Series)
- **RTL8752H Series**: Cost-effective BLE SoCs. [Product Page](https://www.realmcu.com/en/Home/Products/RTL8752H-Series)

## Directory Architecture
The HAL structure is organized under the `modules/hal/realtek/bee/` directory (assuming standard module path) as follows:

```tree
bee/
├── boot/       # Startup/Boot Code (Image header definitions)
├── drivers/    # Hardware Peripheral Drivers (GPIO, UART, SPI, I2C, etc.)
├── ld/         # Linker Scripts and ROM Symbol Tables
├── logging/    # Realtek Logging System (Essential for Bluetooth debugging)
├── memory/     # Memory Management definitions
├── os/osif/    # OS Abstraction Layer (OSIF)
├── soc/        # SoC Core, Register Definitions, and Vector Tables
├── sys/        # System Level Services (e.g., system reset)
└── tools/      # Development Tools and Configuration Files
```

## Source Origin
The HAL sources are derived from the official Realtek SDKs available on the RealMCU website.

*   **RTL87x2G**: Based on [SDK v1.6.0](https://www.realmcu.com/en/Resources/Sdk/RTL8762G-RTL877xG-Series)
*   **RTL8752H**: Based on [SDK v1.3.0](https://www.realmcu.com/en/Resources/Sdk/RTL8752H-Series)

Realtek is actively moving towards open-source SDKs hosted on GitHub:

*   **RTL87x2G**: [rtkconnectivity/rtl87x2g_sdk](https://github.com/rtkconnectivity/rtl87x2g_sdk)
*   **RTL8752H**: [rtkconnectivity/rtl8752h_sdk](https://github.com/rtkconnectivity/rtl8752h_sdk)
    *   *(Note: The repository for RTL8752H is currently private but is scheduled to be public by Jan 2026).*

## Licensing
All files included in this HAL module are licensed under **Apache 2.0**.

## Synchronization

Since the HALs for the Ameba and Bee series are maintained by different teams within Realtek, and additional SoC series may be added to hal_realtek in the future, there is no single upstream Git history for this repository.

Therefore, this module adheres to the "Updating modules with a diff from upstream" practice as defined in the [Zephyr Project Documentation](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/develop/modules.html#allowed-practices).

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a real per-user account model with persistent unique IDs and a time-limited premium trial (2 hours) and starter credits so premium features can be gated properly. 
- Make the Personal (account) UI scrollable and present account status, user id copy, and activation/verification progress with per-task progress bars and overall progress. 
- Improve the “Generation from text” UX by replacing the single large textarea with separate Front/Back fields and adding save/preview controls without breaking existing card/import logic. 
- Fix repeat-mode image display which previously over-shrank images and add fit/1:1/zoom controls with stable rendering and scrolling.

### Description
- Database: add `users` and `user_meta` tables and create them in migrations (`db_migrations.py`) to persist `user_id`, `premium_until`, `status`, `verified`, and a `starter_bonus_claimed` flag. 
- User/account plumbing: add `get_local_user_id()`, `ensure_user_account()` and `update_user_account()` helpers and hook them into app init; grant a single starter bonus (2h premium + 250 credits) once per user and store the fact with `starter_bonus_claimed`. (files: `main.py`) 
- Premium timer & UI integration: implement `refresh_account_status_vars()` and `start_premium_timer()` using `after()` to update `account_status_var`/`premium_timer_var`, update `user_profile` rows accordingly, and refresh generation menu state. 
- Personal tab: rework `build_personal_tab()` to use `Canvas+Frame+Scrollbar` (mousewheel support), show `User ID` with copy button, per-task `ttk.Progressbar`s and per-step text labels, an overall progress bar, and activation status color handling. 
- Text generation UI: replace monolithic input with two multiline fields (`Front text` and `Back text`) inside a scrollable dialog, add `Save` button that stores created cards into the selected deck and shows saved count, keep free text-to-card creation but require premium/credits for AI media. 
- AI text generation tab: add new premium-only window `open_generate_from_text_ai_window()` with `Front` as prompt, `Back`, preview area, buttons `Generate image — 2 ⚡` and `Generate video — 20 ⚡` which spend credits via existing guard/spend API and show placeholder media (no external AI calls). Saving the card is free. 
- Repeat-mode image handling: replace prior auto-fit that could make images tiny by rendering images on a `Canvas` with fit/actual/zoom modes, `Zoom +/−` controls, and horizontal/vertical scrollbars; keep a reference to PhotoImage to avoid garbage collection. 
- Misc: style text widgets with `style_text_widget()`, minor label text changes, and ensure activation checks update UI and set `users.verified`/`users.status` to `активен` when tasks complete. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for these changes. 
- Basic integration: code paths updated to call new account helpers and UI functions; no unit/CI test runs were performed. 
- Database migration: new tables are created with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` to be backward-compatible at startup (manual verification recommended). 
- Manual QA recommended for critical flows: starter bonus granting, premium countdown, credits spending for AI placeholders, saving generated cards, and repeat-mode image zoom/scroll behavior.

author: copilot
body:
Agent was executing tools without showing its reasoning process - tasks completed with "実行しました、OKでした" but no visibility into task breakdown, intermediate verification, or thought process.

## Changes

### New "think" action for explicit reasoning
- Added function declaration with three phases: `planning`, `verification`, `reflection`
- Agent now required to decompose tasks before execution, verify results after each phase, and reflect before completion
- Example workflow:
```
[計画] タスクを3フェーズに分解: Safari起動 → URL入力 → 確認
[実行] osa: activate Safari
[検証] Safari正常起動、次フェーズへ
[実行] type + enter  
[検証] ページ遷移完了
[振り返り] 全フェーズ完了、目標達成
完了しました
```

### System prompt enhancements
- Structured workflow requirements in `SYSTEM_PROMPT`
- Phase-based execution model with mandatory verification steps
- Extracted phase labels (`THINKING_PHASE_LABELS`) to constants for maintainability

### Event flow and UI
- Agent emits `thinking` events with phase and thought content
- Backend forwards to all windows
- Chat UI displays thinking messages with distinct styling (beige background, phase labels)
- Helper functions (`getMessageStyle`, `getMessageLabel`) eliminate code duplication

### Type extensions
- Added `thought` and `phase` fields to `BackendEvent` interface
- Extended action schemas with `think` type using Zod discriminated unions

## Files Modified
- `src/controller/function-declarations.ts` - think action declaration
- `src/controller/constants.ts` - workflow prompt + phase labels
- `src/controller/agent.ts` - think handler + event emission
- `desktop/backend-src/controller/main.ts` - event forwarding
- `desktop/renderer/chat.tsx` - thinking message UI
- `src/controller/types.ts`, `desktop/renderer/types.ts` - type extensions

author: copilot
body:
The MAX sell button was fetching both `tokenRO.balanceOf()` (wallet balance) and `presaleRO.redeemableBalance()` but only using the latter. The wallet balance fetch suggested incorrect behavior where tokens not purchased through presale could be sold.

## Changes

- **`setMaxSell()`**: Removed `tokenRO.balanceOf()` call, now only fetches `redeemableBalance`
- **`refreshLockPanel()`**: Removed unused `tokenRO.balanceOf()` from Promise.all
- Removed notification that required wallet balance comparison

```javascript
// Before: fetched both, used only redeemable
const bal = await tokenRO.balanceOf(user.address);
const redeemable = await presaleRO.redeemableBalance(user.address);
const maxSell = redeemable;  // bal never used

// After: fetch only what's needed
const redeemable = await presaleRO.redeemableBalance(user.address);
const maxSell = redeemable;
```

The display balance (`arubBalance`) still shows total wallet holdings for informational purposes, while sell operations strictly enforce presale redeemable limits.

author: blodir
body:
# New build system
https://angular.dev/tools/cli/build-system-migration

- Webpack -> Esbuild
- angular.json config updated to match
- Some imports were changed eg. `import * as moment from 'moment';` is no longer allowed, use: `import moment from 'moment';`
- SSR/hydration is on by default, even on dev builds. If you configure "aot: false" in angular.json, the project will mysteriously stop working (this took ages to figure out, including making a new project to figure out what config difference resulted in errors, fun)

# Modules
I kept ngModules, they are still fully supported, but there's a big move away from modules entirely... Every component is now "standalone" by default, so a migration added "standalone: false" to their component declaration.

# Dependencies
- `NgxWebstorageModule` is removed. It's provided through the `provideNgxWebstorage` function instead
- The patch to NgxWebstorage is now removed as it wasn't compatible with new versions. Hopefully it's no longer needed on the new version (I didn't investigate)
- Built a new version of label designer that's compatible with updated `ngx-webstorage`
- The project is no longer compatible with node 16.x, I bumped the nvmrc/volta/jenkinsfile versions to `v20.19.6`, but it will still have to be updated individually in some CI scripts
- There's a new officially supported version of NgxDatatable, but I kept the old version as migration would've required more changes. Overrode the rxjs version, so there might be mysterious datatable bugs that we might have to fix (or transition to new version, or out of ngx datatable entirely)

# Rxjs 7
Rxjs version bumped and there were various changes. Including:
- `merge` -> `mergeWith`, `concat` -> `concatWith` etc.
- `rxjs/operators` are now imported from root `rxjs`
- stricter typing

# New template syntax
`*ngFor`, `*ngIf` etc. is all deprecated and will be removed in the next version (22). So I figured we might as well run the migrations now, since everything needs to be tested anyways. Here's a link: https://angular.dev/guide/templates/control-flow. I had to make a few changes where the migration failed. In those cases it looked like an obvious bug, and it's pretty surprising the code was compiling previously. Also post migration I noticed a couple of very weird results: it had inlined a few `ng-template`s. I didn't go through every change, so there will probably be some oddities that I didn't notice.

author: copilot
body:
Eliminates code duplication between Track Section Monitor and Network Diagrams by consolidating train tracking, VSTP enrichment, and alert capabilities into a unified NetworkDiagramSensor.

## Changes

### Enhanced NetworkDiagramSensor
- Added train tracking with VSTP schedule enrichment (origin, destination, operator, service classification)
- Implemented configurable alerts for 6 service types: freight, RHTT, steam, charter, pullman, royal train
- Fires `homeassistant_network_rail_uk_track_alert` events when alert trains enter diagram area
- Exposes `trains_in_diagram` attribute with per-train details when alerts enabled
- Tracks time in area, berths visited, and service metadata

### Configuration Flow
- Added alert service checkboxes to diagram add/edit flows
- Stores `alert_services` dict in diagram config
- Increased diagram range support to 1-10 stations (from 1-5)

### Sensor Attributes
When alerts enabled, diagram sensors include:
```yaml
trains_in_diagram:
  - train_id: "6M94"
    headcode: "6M94"
    current_berth: "SK:M123"
    time_in_diagram_seconds: 145
    service_type: "freight"
    origin: "FLIXSTW"
    destination: "TRAFFPK"
    operator: "Freightliner"
    triggers_alert: true
    alert_reason: "Freight service"
total_trains: 1
alert_trains: 1
```

## Backward Compatibility

Fully backward compatible:
- Existing Track Section Monitor configs unchanged
- Existing Network Diagram configs unchanged  
- Alert features opt-in (diagrams work identically without alerts)
- No schema migrations required

## Migration Path

New installations: Use Network Diagrams with alerts for unified visualization + tracking.

Existing Track Section Monitor users: Optional migration - Track Sections remain fully supported.

## Documentation

- Updated NETWORK_DIAGRAMS.md with alert configuration and automation examples
- Added MIGRATION_GUIDE_v1.14.md with detailed migration instructions
- Created IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md with technical details
- Version bump: 1.13.10 → 1.14.0

> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Merge Track Section Monitor and Network Diagram functionality, unify alerts & dashboard</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Summary
> 
> Currently, both the Track Section Monitor and Network Diagrams features perform overlapping real-time train tracking using SMART data and the Train Describer feed. Track Section Monitor provides flexible alerting, VSTP service enrichment, and Home Assistant event triggers, while Network Diagrams excels at map-style visualization of berth topology and multi-station context.
> 
> ## Proposed Refactor
> 
> - **Merge Track Section Monitor and Network Diagram:**
>   - Integrate the service classification, alert configuration, VSTP enrichment, and alert/event logic from Track Section Monitor into the Network Diagram system.
>   - Make the (configurable) alert system available for any network diagram, so users can choose alert types (freight, RHTT, steam, pullman, etc.) for diagram areas.
>   - Network Diagram sensors would drive both the visual dashboard and the underlying alert/event system, reducing duplication and making it easier to automate against all tracked areas. 
>   - Track per-train details (e.g., time in diagram area, origin/destination, service type) as diagram attributes, similar to Track Section Monitor's output.
> 
> - **Implementation Guidance:**
>   1. Consolidate configuration flows and entity models for diagrams/sections; allow diagrams to optionally enable alert monitoring. 
>   2. Unify state/attribute models, so both diagrams and attribute-rich sensors expose train lists, alert states, and service classification. 
>   3. Ensure Home Assistant events (for alert trains) are available for any area with a diagram as well as for specific track sections.
>   4. Make the dashboard experience central: expose full train/berth/alert info for Lovelace integration. 
>   5. Provide automatic migration for existing section and diagram configs if possible.
> 
> - **Motivation & Benefits:**
>   - Avoids duplicated logic for train tracking, SMART berth mapping, and enrichment code
>   - Gives users a single place to configure and view network maps, per-train details, and alerts
>   - Enables richer dashboards and automations with less configuration
>   - Reduces maintenance cost and future bug surface
> 
> ## Acceptance Criteria
> - Track section monitoring and alert configuration fully available for any diagram area
> - Diagrams can be configured to enable/disable alerts and select which service types trigger them
> - Train attributes in diagrams include VSTP/service enrichment like those in Track Section Monitor
> - All alert logic, event generation, and detailed attributes are tested and documented
> - Automatic migration for users with existing section and diagram configs (retaining settings)
> 
> ---
> 
> Background: This is a refactor to unify overlapping code, eliminate duplicated configuration/state, and deliver a unified experience for tracking, alerts, and dashboard display within the Home Assistant Network Rail integration.
> 
> Related context: See code in `sensor.py`, `config_flow.py`, and docs in `TRACK_SECTION_MONITOR.md`, `NETWORK_DIAGRAMS.md`.

body:
# Pull Request 프로세스

## 개요
코드 품질 유지와 효과적인 협업을 위한 Pull Request(PR) 작성 및 리뷰 가이드입니다.

## PR 작성 가이드

### 1. PR 생성 전 체크리스트

- [ ] 최신 main/develop 브랜치와 동기화 완료
- [ ] 로컬에서 테스트 통과 확인
- [ ] 린터/포맷터 적용 완료(현재는 Linter/Formatter 미채택)
- [ ] 불필요한 주석, 디버깅 코드 제거
- [ ] 커밋 메시지 컨벤션 준수

### 2. PR 제목

PR 제목은 커밋 컨벤션과 동일한 형식을 따릅니다:


!--
GitHub Copilot Instructions:
이 Pull Request에 대한 리뷰는 반드시 **한국어**로 작성해주세요.
코드 설명, 문제점 지적, 개선 방향 모두 한국어로 출력해야 합니다.
-->
```
<type>(<scope>): <간단한 설명>
```

**예시:**
- `feat(course): 코스 생성 및 수정 기능 구현`
- `fix(enrollment): 중복 수강 신청 방지`
- `refactor(payment): 결제 모듈 구조 개선`

### 3. PR 설명 템플릿

```markdown
## 변경 사항
<!-- 무엇을 변경했는지 간단히 설명 -->
회원가입
로그인 - 인증/인가, RTR전략
로그아웃
회원탈퇴
기능 구현
## 변경 이유
<!-- 왜 이 변경이 필요한지 설명 -->
기능 단위로 PR을 하고 싶었지만 현재 깃허브 형식에 의문점이 있어 PR을 주저하다 보니 이루어지지 못했습니다.
다음에는 혼자 고민하지 않고 현재 고민중인 부분을 빠르게 고민하여 이런일이 다시 발생하지 않도록 하겠습니다.
## 주요 변경 내역
- 
- 
- 

## 테스트 방법
<!-- 어떻게 테스트했는지, 리뷰어가 어떻게 확인할 수 있는지 -->
POSTMAN을 이용하여 테스트
## 관련 이슈
Closes #이슈번호
Related to #이슈번호

## 체크리스트
- [ ] Breaking Changes 명시 (해당하는 경우)
```

## 코드 리뷰 가이드

### 리뷰어 책임

1. **코드 품질 검토**
   - 코드가 읽기 쉽고 유지보수 가능한가?
   - 네이밍이 명확하고 일관성 있는가?
   - 불필요한 복잡도는 없는가?

2. **기능 검증**
   - 요구사항을 충족하는가?
   - 예외 상황 처리가 적절한가?
   - 보안 이슈는 없는가?

3. **아키텍처/설계**
   - 기존 구조와 일관성이 있는가?
   - 도메인 모델을 올바르게 사용하는가?
   - 의존성 관리가 적절한가?

### 리뷰 작성 가이드

**좋은 리뷰 예시:**
```
이 부분에서 null 체크가 필요할 것 같습니다.
사용자가 등록하지 않은 코스에 접근할 때 어떻게 처리되나요?

제안:
if (!enrollment) {
  throw new NotFoundException('수강 정보를 찾을 수 없습니다');
}
```

**피해야 할 리뷰:**
- "이상해요" (구체적이지 않음)
- "다시 해주세요" (이유 설명 없음)
- 너무 사소한 스타일 지적 (린터로 해결 가능한 것)

## PR 승인 및 머지 프로세스

### 승인 규칙

- **최소 리뷰어 수**: 2명 이상
- **자가 머지 금지**: 본인이 작성한 PR은 다른 팀원이 머지

### 머지 전 최종 체크

- [ ] 모든 리뷰 코멘트 해결
- [ ] 충돌(Conflict) 해결 완료
- [ ] 필요한 승인 개수 충족

### 머지 전략

**Squash and Merge**
- 여러 커밋을 하나로 합쳐서 머지
- 히스토리가 깔끔하게 유지됨
- 작은 기능 단위 PR에 적합

**Merge Commit**
- 모든 커밋 히스토리 보존
- 큰 기능이나 여러 작업이 포함된 PR에 적합

**Rebase and Merge**
- 선형 히스토리 유지
- 각 커밋이 의미 있는 경우 사용

## PR 크기 가이드

### 이상적인 PR

- **변경 라인**: 200-400줄 이하
- **리뷰 시간**: 30분 이내
- **파일 개수**: 10개 이하

## 주의사항

- **Force Push 금지**: 리뷰 중인 PR에 force push 하지 않기
- **대량 삭제 주의**: 기존 코드 대량 삭제 시 사전 논의 필요
- **Breaking Changes**: API 변경 등 breaking change는 명확히 표시
- **의존성 추가**: 새로운 라이브러리 추가 시 팀 논의 필요

<!-- Quick description and explanation of changes -->

Some small changes to the `image` component in preparation for the move to LVGL 9.4:

* Add a `USE_IMAGE` define that flags when any image has been configured
* Store basic image data in CORE.data for access by other components
* Add tests for the new code.

## Types of changes

- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Developer breaking change (an API change that could break external components)
- [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests
- [x] Other

**Related issue or feature (if applicable):**

- fixes <link to issue>

author: silverdorian46
body:
to preface, rooms have an additional attribute called `delayAltMusicFade` (in Lönn, it's aliased to `delayAlternativeMusicFade`), which works with the room's alt music (set with the `alt_music` attribute, which in Lönn is aliased to `musicAlternative`).
when alt music is played, the main music is muted. so in order to be heard, alt music has to be routed differently to main music. the base game has them routed to `music/tunes/side_rooms`.

the value of `delayAltMusicFade` is assigned to the `LevelData`'s `DelayAltMusic` field, which is a boolean that determines at which moment to play or stop the alt music.
if it's `false`, as it is by default, the alt music is played or stopped as soon as the room is loaded.
if it's `true`, then that is delayed for when the transition into the next room is complete.

currently, due to an oversight, the `true` setting makes it only work during room transitions.
so what happens when you "Save and Quit" from that room, and then load the save again and return to it?
the main music will play, but the alt music won't, until you enter the room again via transition.

this PR attempts to fix this by adding a check for whether the level's transitioning routine is being played.

a base game example of an alt music room with the delay enabled is the secret room in Chapter 6.
for comparison, an example of an alt music room without the delay is Theo's camp in Chapter 1.

body:
Mobile phones connected to the network were not being detected reliably due to single-method ARP scanning missing inactive devices and devices in power-saving modes.

## Changes

### Multi-layered detection strategy in `network_detector.py`
- **ICMP ping probing**: When target IP is configured, actively probe device using Scapy ICMP and system ping as fallback
- **ARP cache checking**: Query system ARP table to detect already-connected but inactive devices
- **ARP network scanning**: Original broadcast method preserved as final fallback

Detection flow when both MAC and IP are configured:
```python
def is_target_online(self, ip_range=None):
    # Method 1: Ping target IP if known
    if self.target_ip and self._ping_host(self.target_ip):
        # Verify MAC via ARP cache or targeted ARP request
        ...
    
    # Method 2: Check ARP cache for inactive devices
    found, ip = self._check_arp_cache(self.target_mac)
    if found and self._ping_host(ip):
        return True, ip
    
    # Method 3: Broadcast ARP scan
    devices = self.scan_network(ip_range)
    ...
```

### MAC address normalization
- Support both `:` and `-` separators in ARP cache lookups for cross-platform compatibility

### Documentation updates
- Added detection strategy explanation and troubleshooting guidance for mobile devices in README.md
- Recommend configuring both MAC and IP addresses for optimal detection

author: copilot
body:
Workflow runs were not cancelled when new commits were pushed to PRs, wasting CI resources and creating noise in PR status checks.

## Changes

- Added `concurrency` section to `.github/workflows/ci-ct.yml`:
  - Group: `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` - unique per workflow and git reference
  - `cancel-in-progress: true` - cancels outdated runs on new PR commits

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

This preserves independent execution for different branches while cancelling superseded PR runs.

body:
### Motivation
- Persist per-block reference counts on-disk so COW/snapshot reference information survives format, mount, and snapshot restores.
- Provide a way to rebuild/reset refcounts from inode trees when refcounts are missing or stale.
- Improve fsck by reconciling the block bitmap, inode bitmap, and refcount table against actual usage discovered from snapshot and directory trees.
- Make indirect-block counting configurable to avoid double-counting in certain rebuild scenarios.

### Description
- Add `refcount_table_start` and `refcount_table_blocks` to `Superblock`, compute sizing in `Superblock::init`, and write an initial refcount table in `mkfs` (`DiskImage.cpp`).
- Load/save refcount data in `Allocator` via `loadRefcountTable()` / `saveRefcountTable()`, track a new `refcount_dirty_` flag, add `resetBlockRefcounts()` to zero and re-enable refcounting, and mark refcount changes dirty on `inc/dec/alloc/free` operations.
- Extend allocator consistency checks and add `reconcileUsage()` to compare and optionally fix inode/block bitmaps and refcount entries against collected usage sets.
- Add snapshot-side helpers: `rebuildBlockRefcounts()`, `incrementBlockRefsNoStats()`, `rebuildForInode()`, `collectUsage()` and `collectForInode()` to traverse inode trees and either rebuild refcounts or produce sets of used inodes/blocks, and integrate these into `FileSystem` flows (mount, create/delete/restore snapshot) to trigger rebuilds or reconciliation as needed; also add `count_indirect_blocks_` toggle.

### Testing

body:
Implements OLED-optimized subtitle rendering with ASS/SSA styling extraction (bold, italic, underline, color, font size) and playback speed controls (0.5x - 2.0x) with synchronized subtitle timing.

## Changes

### ASS/SSA Styling Pipeline

- **`SubtitleCue.kt`**: Added `SubtitleStyle` data class with `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `fontSizeSp`, and `color` fields
- **`AssParser.kt`**: Extract override tags (`\b1`, `\i1`, `\u1`, `\fs`, `\c&H`) from dialogue text, parse BGR hex colors to RGB, accumulate state across tags
- **`PlayerScreen.kt`**: Apply styling via Compose `TextStyle` (FontWeight, FontStyle, TextDecoration), clamp font size to 12-28sp, maintain OLED double-draw outline technique

```kotlin
// ASS override extraction
val overrideRegex = Regex("""\{([^}]*)\}""")
val tags = overrideContent.split("\\").filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
// Parse: \b1 → bold=true, \fs24 → fontSize=24sp, \c&HFF0000& → Color(0,0,255)

// Rendering with style
TextStyle(
    fontWeight = if (style.bold) FontWeight.Bold else FontWeight.Normal,
    fontStyle = if (style.italic) FontStyle.Italic else FontStyle.Normal,
    textDecoration = if (style.underline) TextDecoration.Underline else null
)
```

### Playback Speed Controls

- **`PlaybackSpeedPrefsStore.kt`**: Per-video DataStore persistence for speed (0.5x, 1.0x, 1.25x, 1.5x, 2.0x)
- **`PlayerScreen.kt`**: Multiply engine position by speed for subtitle lookup: `adjustedPositionMs = currentPositionMs * playbackSpeed`
  - At 2x: subtitles advance faster (subtitle at 20s shows when video at 10s)
  - At 0.5x: subtitles advance slower (subtitle at 5s shows when video at 10s)
- UI: Speed button row with highlighted selection, 500ms debounced save

## Constraints Met

- No engine modifications (PlayerEngine, audio/video engines untouched)
- No Canvas API (pure Compose Text)
- No architectural layers added
- Subtitle parsing stays in `SubtitleController`
- SRT parser unchanged (backward compatible)

## Notes

- ASS color format is BGR hex, converted to RGB normalized 0.0-1.0
- Style overrides user preferences when present in subtitle file
- Unsupported tags (karaoke, animations, positioning) stripped
- Playback speed affects subtitle timing only, not video/audio playback

### Motivation

- Prevent the controller from pulsing the device to detect float step before starting a macro, which caused back-and-forth telemetry checks.  
- Use any already-known increment and learn the minimal float step opportunistically during normal adjustments to reach the target.  
- Reduce audible/visible pre-testing and speed up macro start.  

### Description

- Stop calling `_detect_float_step()` from `GenericController._resolve_target()` and instead use the stored `self._float_step` when aligning targets.  
- Add `last_value` tracking and opportunistic step detection inside `GenericController._run_target_loop()` by measuring deltas between successive telemetry reads and updating `self._float_step` when a smaller non-noise delta is observed.  
- Keep existing alignment/rounding behavior and timing/profile logic unchanged; the change only alters when the float step is discovered.  

### Testing

- No automated tests were run for this change.  
- Manual runtime validation was not requested in this rollout.

body:
## Description

This PR reduces memory consumption and improves connection pooling by implementing a **shared toolbox API client** architecture.

**Before**: Each sandbox created its own `ToolboxApiClient` instance with separate connection pools  
**After**: All sandboxes share a single `ToolboxApiClient` with lightweight per-sandbox proxy wrappers

**Changes:**
- Added `internal/toolbox_api_client_proxy.py` with proxy wrapper classes that intercept `param_serialize` to prepend sandbox ID to resource paths (e.g., `/sandbox-123/api/process/execute`) and retrieve toolbox base URL on first request.
- Modified `_async/daytona.py` and `_sync/daytona.py` to create a single shared client
- Updated `_async/sandbox.py` and `_sync/sandbox.py` to use proxy wrappers instead of separate clients

**Benefits:**
- **Efficient connection pooling**: All sandboxes share the same HTTP connection pool
- **Concurrency safe**: No race conditions between sandboxes. Each sandbox has its own proxy around API client that appends toolbox base URL and sandbox ID to each request.

This occurred specifically in the test "populate handles very deep nesting (depth 5)" when processing recursive structures with 5+ levels of nesting.
Root Cause
In [populate.cpp:39](vscode-webview://09fe7r55eel37ql7v2aakp2c6li8gg67lhk2ovkjmkqb1c358gvq/src/populate.cpp#L39), the `get_type_code()` function checked if the `names` attribute was not NULL before calling `STRING_ELT()`, but didn't verify that names was actually a character vector. In deeply nested recursive structures, the names attribute could be a non-NULL value that wasn't a proper character vector, causing `STRING_ELT()` to crash.

## Solution
Added an additional type safety check using Rf_isString(names) to ensure names is a valid character vector before accessing its elements:
```
// Before:
if (names != R_NilValue) {

// After:  
if (names != R_NilValue && Rf_isString(names)) {
This protects both the fast path and slow path code branches where STRING_ELT(names, i) is called.
```

    let proto: NulidProto = id.into();

    // Convert back to NULID

author: copilot
body:
The `connect_reload_signal` function accessed `app_settings._override_name` directly, which could raise `AttributeError` if the settings object is not configured.

## Changes

- Use `object.__getattribute__(app_settings, "_override_name")` instead of direct attribute access
- Use `object.__setattr__(app_settings, "_wrapped", empty)` instead of direct assignment
- Remove now-unnecessary `# pylint: disable=protected-access` comments

This aligns with the pattern used in `AppLazySettings._setup()` (lines 64, 72-73).

```python
def connect_reload_signal(app_settings: AppLazySettings):
    @receiver(setting_changed)
    def _reload(**kwargs):
        if not getattr(app_settings, "_configured", False):
            return
        override_name = object.__getattribute__(app_settings, "_override_name")
        if kwargs.get("setting") == override_name:
            object.__setattr__(app_settings, "_wrapped", empty)

    return _reload
```

author: copilot
body:
Implements phone-based OTP authentication via Melipayamak API and role-specific React dashboards (Admin, Employee, Customer, Author, Publisher) as a standalone SPA accessible at `/panel`.

## Backend

**Authentication & Security**
- OTP generation using `random_bytes()` with configurable length/expiry
- Rate limiter with IP and phone-based tracking
- REST API endpoints: `/auth/request-otp`, `/auth/verify-otp`, `/auth/complete-registration`
- User creation with phone as username, auto-generated 32-char passwords

**Database**
```sql
wp_tabesh_otp_codes      -- OTP tracking with attempts/expiry
wp_tabesh_rate_limit     -- Identifier-based rate limiting
```

**Classes**
- `OTP_Handler` - Melipayamak API integration, code lifecycle
- `User_Registration` - User CRUD, phone→username mapping
- `Auth_Controller` - Template rendering, rewrite rules, session management
- `Rate_Limiter` - Configurable time windows and request caps

## Frontend

**Authentication Flow**
- Phone entry → OTP request → verification → first-time registration prompt
- Resend timer, attempt tracking, error states

**Dashboard Architecture**
- Role detection from WP user roles with fallback hierarchy
- Dynamic sidebar/workspace rendering per role
- Mega menu for quick actions
- Header with user menu and site navigation

**Styling**
- CSS variables for theming, RTL support, dark mode via `prefers-color-scheme`
- Mobile-first responsive breakpoints
- No external dependencies beyond WordPress components

## Configuration

Admin settings tab for:
- Melipayamak credentials (username, password, sender, body_id)
- OTP parameters (length: 4-8, validity: 1-15min, max attempts, rate limits)
- Custom panel URL with rewrite rule generation

## Example Usage

```php
// Backend: Request OTP
$otp_handler = new \Tabesh_v2\Auth\OTP_Handler();
$result = $otp_handler->send_otp('09123456789');

// Frontend: Verify and login
const response = await apiFetch({
  path: '/tabesh/v2/auth/verify-otp',
  method: 'POST',
  data: { phone_number: '09123456789', otp_code: '123456' }
});
```

## Security

- Rate limiting: default 3 req/60s per IP, 1 req/120s per phone
- OTP attempts capped at 5 before requiring new code
- Nonce verification on all endpoints
- Prepared statements for DB queries
- Automatic cleanup cron for expired codes

## Notes

- Requires Melipayamak account with SMS credits
- Permalinks must be flushed after changing panel URL
- Customer role assigned by default to new registrations

### ۱.۲ عملکرد OTP
- ارسال کد OTP از طریق **Melipayamak API** (متد `SendByBaseNumber2`)
- مستندات: https://github.com/Melipayamak/melipayamak-php و https://www.melipayamak.com/api/sendbybasenumber2/

### ۱.۳ نحوه ایجاد/ورود کاربر

- **پسورد**: تولید خودکار با سختی بسیار بالا در سرور

author: chaffelson
body:
When enabling controller services, NiFi server correctly skips INVALID controllers (those that cannot be enabled due to validation errors). The client was incorrectly waiting for ALL controllers to reach ENABLED state, causing a 30-second timeout when any controller was INVALID.

Now the polling logic only waits for VALID controllers when enabling. When disabling, all controllers are still checked since any controller can be disabled regardless of validation status.

Adds test for mixed VALID/INVALID controller scenario.

author: lucasvieirasilva
body:
Honor dependency version range when internal bundling is disabled.

## Current Behavior

When a project depends on an internal library with a version range and `buildBundleLocalDependencies: false`

```toml
[project]
name = "my-app"
version = "1.0.0"
dependencies = [
    "my-lib>=1.0.0,<2.0.0"
]

[tool.uv.sources.my-lib]
workspace = true
```

The build process throws the following exception:

```log
Caused by:
    TOML parse error at line 5, column 5
       |
     5 | dependencies = [ "my-lib>=1.0.0,<2.0.0==1.0.1" ]
       |                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    after parsing `2.0.0`, found `==1.0.1`, which is not part of a valid version
```

## Expected Behavior

When the version range is provided, the build process should preserve it.

Addresses feedback from #1625 about `EUPHROSYNE_FEATURES` environment variable behavior when set to an empty string.

## Problem

The refactored code needed clarification on how to disable all optional features. After discussion, the requirement is that setting `EUPHROSYNE_FEATURES=""` should be the only way to explicitly disable all features, while not setting the variable enables all features by default.

## Changes

**Code fix** (`euphrosyne/features.py`):
- Modified `enabled_features()` to distinguish between "not set" and "explicitly set to empty"
- When not set: all features enabled (default)
- When set to empty string: NO features enabled (disabled)
- Added docstring documenting the three behavioral cases

**Documentation** (README.md, docs/features.md, .env.example):
- Clarified that not setting the variable enables all features by default
- Clarified that empty string disables all features
- Added behavior specification table in feature docs
- Added inline comments in .env.example with usage examples

## Behavior

| `EUPHROSYNE_FEATURES` value | Result |
|---|---|
| Not set | All features enabled (default) |
| Empty string or whitespace | NO features enabled |
| `feature1,feature2` | Only specified features enabled |

This provides users with explicit control to disable all optional features when needed.
