🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ preact (10.28.1 → 10.28.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/preactjs/preact)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Preact has JSON VNode Injection issue

Impact

Vulnerability Type: HTML Injection via JSON Type Confusion

Affected Versions: Preact 10.26.5 through 10.28.1

Severity: Low to Medium (see below)

Who is Impacted?

Applications using affected Preact versions are vulnerable if they meet all of the following conditions:

  1. Pass unmodified, unsanitized values from user-modifiable data sources (APIs, databases, local storage, etc.) directly into the render tree
  2. Assume these values are strings but the data source could return actual JavaScript objects instead of JSON strings
  3. The data source either:
    • Fails to perform type sanitization AND blindly stores/returns raw objects interchangeably with strings, OR
    • Is compromised (e.g., poisoned local storage, filesystem, or database)

Technical Details

Preact includes JSON serialization protection to prevent Virtual DOM elements from being constructed from arbitrary JSON. A regression introduced in Preact 10.26.5 caused this protection to be softened. In applications where values from JSON payloads are assumed to be strings and passed unmodified to Preact as children, a specially-crafted JSON payload could be constructed that would be incorrectly treated as a valid VNode. When this chain of failures occurs it can result in HTML injection, which can allow arbitrary script execution if not mitigated by CSP or other means.

Important Notes:

  • This regression was never present in preact-render-to-string
  • This is primarily an "expanded attack surface" issue rather than a standalone vulnerability
  • Exploitation requires either insecure API design (no type validation) or a compromised data source

Patches

Patched Versions:

  • 10.26.10 (for 10.26.x users)
  • 10.27.3 (for 10.27.x users)
  • 10.28.2 (for 10.28.x users)

Users should upgrade to the latest patch version of whatever minor version they are on, which can be done via npm update preact or by installing one of the above versions directly.

The patch versions simply restore the previous strict equality checks that prevent JSON-parsed objects from being treated as valid VNodes.

Mitigations

If you cannot upgrade immediately, implement the following mitigations:

  • Validate input types: Don't accept arbitrary objects as inputs in your API and blindly store them. Enforce strict type contracts at API boundaries.
  • Cast or validate network data: Don't assume strings are strings if your code got them from the network. Always cast to the expected type or validate before rendering.
  • Sanitize external data: Validate that data from external sources (APIs, storage, databases) matches expected types before passing it to preact.
  • Use Content Security Policy (CSP): Implement a strict CSP to prevent inline script execution as a defense-in-depth measure.

References

  • Reporter: YoungGeun Choi
  • Affected Versions: 10.26.5 - 10.28.1
  • Patched Versions: 10.26.10, 10.27.3, 10.28.2

Credits

Preact thanks YoungGeun Choi (Xvezda) for the responsible disclosure of this vulnerability and for providing detailed reproduction steps and proof-of-concept demonstrations.

Timeline

  • 2026-01-04: Initial vulnerability report received
  • 2026-01-05: Clarification requested regarding network/serialization boundary
  • 2026-01-06: Network PoC provided demonstrating real-world exploitatibility
  • 2026-01-06: Hotfix patches released (10.26.10, 10.27.3, 10.28.2)

Recommendation: All users of Preact 10.26.5 through 10.28.1 should upgrade to the appropriate patched version (10.26.10, 10.27.3, or 10.28.2) as soon as possible, and review their applications for proper input validation and sanitization practices.

Release Notes

10.28.2

Fixes

  • Enforce strict equality for VNode object constructors

Does any of this look wrong? Please let us know.

Commits

See the full diff on Github. The new version differs by 3 commits:

  • 10.28.2
  • Strict equality check on constructor (#4985)
  • chore: Adjust TS linting setup (#4982)

## PR Checklist: Submitter

- [ ]   Link to an issue if possible. If there’s no issue, describe what your branch does. Even if there is an issue, a brief description in the PR is still useful.
- [ ]   List any special steps reviewers have to follow to test the PR. For example, adding a local environment variable, creating a local test file, etc.
- [ ]   For extra credit, submit a screen recording like [this one](https://github.com/GSA-TTS/FAC/pull/1821).
- [ ]   Make sure you’ve merged `main` into your branch shortly before creating the PR. (You should also be merging `main` into your branch regularly during development.)
- [ ]   Make sure you’ve accounted for any migrations. When you’re about to create the PR, bring up the application locally and then run `git status | grep migrations`. If there are any results, you probably need to add them to the branch for the PR. Your PR should have only **one** new migration file for each of the component apps, except in rare circumstances; you may need to delete some and re-run `python manage.py makemigrations` to reduce the number to one. (Also, unless in exceptional circumstances, your PR should not delete any migration files.)
- [ ]   Make sure that whatever feature you’re adding has tests that cover the feature. This includes test coverage to make sure that the previous workflow still works, if applicable.
- [ ]   Make sure the full-submission.cy.js [Cypress test](https://github.com/GSA-TTS/FAC/blob/main/docs/testing.md#end-to-end-testing) passes, if applicable.
- [ ]   Do manual testing locally. Our tests are not good enough yet to allow us to skip this step. If that’s not applicable for some reason, check this box.
- [ ]   Verify that no Git surgery was necessary, or, if it was necessary at any point, repeat the testing after it’s finished.
- [ ]   Once a PR is merged, keep an eye on it until it’s deployed to dev, and do enough testing on dev to verify that it deployed successfully, the feature works as expected, and the happy path for the broad feature area (such as submission) still works.
- [ ]   Ensure that prior to merging, the working branch is up to date with main and the terraform plan is what you expect.

The larger the PR, the stricter we should be about these points.

author: akre54
body:
## Summary

- Introduces GraphExecutor with topological sorting and cycle detection for cleaner execution management
- Adds GraphScope for scope-based control flow execution (ForEach patterns)
- Adds external `compute()` function that operates on operators (not a method on Operator class)
- Adds `dirty` flag to Operator base class for change tracking
- Adds ForEachBeginOp, ForEachEndOp, ForEachMetaOp for iteration control flow (Houdini-style)
- Fields now mark their owning operator as dirty on value changes

## ForEach Operators

The new ForEach operators follow the Houdini pattern:

- **ForEachBeginOp**: Receives data array, outputs `item`, `index`, `total` - executor sets these during iteration
- **ForEachEndOp**: Collects results from each iteration into output array
- **ForEachMetaOp**: Access accumulator and iteration metadata (`initialValue`, `currentValue` → `accumulator`, `isFirst`, `isLast`)

The graph executor is responsible for managing iteration state and setting values on operators during execution. The body of the ForEach is a group node wrapping all nodes in the scope.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify GraphExecutor creates instances correctly
- [ ] Verify topological sort produces correct order
- [ ] Verify cycle detection works
- [ ] Test ForEachBeginOp, ForEachEndOp, ForEachMetaOp creation and fields
- [ ] Verify dirty flag propagation through fields

# Description

This pull request updates the development container configuration and refines dependency management for the project. The main focus is on improving how the dev container sets up user permissions and installs PowerShell dependencies, as well as updating the format and versions of module dependencies.

author: hansl
body:
Move the following to `JsString` (from `JsStr`):

- `get` and `get_expect` now return `JsString`. Uses `code_point_at()` instead of `get(usize)`
- Move the display types to using a ref to the `JsString` being displayed. Using a `JsString` reference instead of a clone makes it clearer that calling `string.display()` should be temporary (and has a lifetime).
- Move trim to `JsString` and return `JsString` directly.
- Have the code points iterator be part of the `JsString` API and its `vtable`.
- Add inlines and other small time optimizations, like `trim()` not slicing twice.
- This results in less conversions from JsStr to JsString. It's more performant because creating a `JsString` from a slice is as fast (thanks to `SliceString`) than a `JsStr` on a slice, but creating a `JsString` from it is faster now.

The end goal is to get rid of `JsStr` in its current form.

- Ensure cluster-backed support is only granted when the glossator JSON contains a real `DEFINITION` and is not marked `REJECTED`.
- Prevent non-JSON glossator payloads or raw text from being treated as valid definitions.
- Centralize detection of `REJECTED` markers so downstream support/boosting logic only uses accepted definitions.
- Make evidence-derived boosting and filtering more conservative and consistent with repository parsing logic.

### Description
- Replace `_cluster_has_definition` to return true only when ``_extract_glossator_definition(glossator_def)`` yields a non-`None` value.
- Update `_extract_glossator_definition` to avoid returning raw non-JSON text and to only accept parsed glossator JSON definitions.
- Add `_glossator_payload_rejected` to detect `REJECTED` / `rejected` markers and have `_definition_from_glossator_json` return `None` for rejected payloads and only check `"DEFINITION"/"Definition"/"definition"` keys.
- Remove the prior `_first_cluster_raw_definition` and `_first_non_empty` helpers and rely on the stricter glossator JSON extraction used by callers such as `_build_support_lookup`, `_build_evidence_ngrams`, and `_compile_support_stats`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change.
- No test failures reported (no tests run).
- Behavior impact covered by code review of callers that use `_cluster_has_definition`.
- Recommend running existing unit tests and evidence parsing integration tests to validate effects on support/boosting logic.

author: depfu[bot]
body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ preact (10.27.2 → 10.27.3) · [Repo](https://github.com/preactjs/preact)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Preact has JSON VNode Injection issue

Impact

Vulnerability Type: HTML Injection via JSON Type Confusion

Affected Versions: Preact 10.26.5 through 10.28.1

Severity: Low to Medium (see below)

Who is Impacted?

Applications using affected Preact versions are vulnerable if they meet all of the following conditions:

  1. Pass unmodified, unsanitized values from user-modifiable data sources (APIs, databases, local storage, etc.) directly into the render tree
  2. Assume these values are strings but the data source could return actual JavaScript objects instead of JSON strings
  3. The data source either:
    • Fails to perform type sanitization AND blindly stores/returns raw objects interchangeably with strings, OR
    • Is compromised (e.g., poisoned local storage, filesystem, or database)

Technical Details

Preact includes JSON serialization protection to prevent Virtual DOM elements from being constructed from arbitrary JSON. A regression introduced in Preact 10.26.5 caused this protection to be softened. In applications where values from JSON payloads are assumed to be strings and passed unmodified to Preact as children, a specially-crafted JSON payload could be constructed that would be incorrectly treated as a valid VNode. When this chain of failures occurs it can result in HTML injection, which can allow arbitrary script execution if not mitigated by CSP or other means.

Important Notes:

  • This regression was never present in preact-render-to-string
  • This is primarily an "expanded attack surface" issue rather than a standalone vulnerability
  • Exploitation requires either insecure API design (no type validation) or a compromised data source

Patches

Patched Versions:

  • 10.26.10 (for 10.26.x users)
  • 10.27.3 (for 10.27.x users)
  • 10.28.2 (for 10.28.x users)

Users should upgrade to the latest patch version of whatever minor version they are on, which can be done via npm update preact or by installing one of the above versions directly.

The patch versions simply restore the previous strict equality checks that prevent JSON-parsed objects from being treated as valid VNodes.

Mitigations

If you cannot upgrade immediately, implement the following mitigations:

  • Validate input types: Don't accept arbitrary objects as inputs in your API and blindly store them. Enforce strict type contracts at API boundaries.
  • Cast or validate network data: Don't assume strings are strings if your code got them from the network. Always cast to the expected type or validate before rendering.
  • Sanitize external data: Validate that data from external sources (APIs, storage, databases) matches expected types before passing it to preact.
  • Use Content Security Policy (CSP): Implement a strict CSP to prevent inline script execution as a defense-in-depth measure.

References

  • Reporter: YoungGeun Choi
  • Affected Versions: 10.26.5 - 10.28.1
  • Patched Versions: 10.26.10, 10.27.3, 10.28.2

Credits

Preact thanks YoungGeun Choi (Xvezda) for the responsible disclosure of this vulnerability and for providing detailed reproduction steps and proof-of-concept demonstrations.

Timeline

  • 2026-01-04: Initial vulnerability report received
  • 2026-01-05: Clarification requested regarding network/serialization boundary
  • 2026-01-06: Network PoC provided demonstrating real-world exploitatibility
  • 2026-01-06: Hotfix patches released (10.26.10, 10.27.3, 10.28.2)

Recommendation: All users of Preact 10.26.5 through 10.28.1 should upgrade to the appropriate patched version (10.26.10, 10.27.3, or 10.28.2) as soon as possible, and review their applications for proper input validation and sanitization practices.

Release Notes

10.27.3

Fixes

  • Enforce strict equality for VNode object constructors

Does any of this look wrong? Please let us know.

Commits

See the full diff on Github. The new version differs by 3 commits:

  • 10.27.3
  • 10.27 strict equality constructor (#4987)
  • 10.27.x

author: openshift-bot
body:
Updating ose-olm-catalogd-container image to be consistent with ART for 4.22
__TLDR__:
Product builds by ART can be configured for different base and builder images than corresponding CI
builds. This automated PR requests a change to CI configuration to align with ART's configuration;
please take steps to merge it quickly or contact ART to coordinate changes.

The configuration in the following ART component metadata is driving this alignment request:
[ose-olm-catalogd.yml](https://github.com/openshift/ocp-build-data/tree/570937d726a49cff29faf4049bf207d12239d612/images/ose-olm-catalogd.yml).

__Detail__:

This repository is out of sync with the downstream product builds for this component. The CI
configuration for at least one image differs from ART's expected product configuration. This should
be addressed to ensure that the component's CI testing accurate reflects what customers will
experience.

Most of these PRs are opened as an ART-driven proposal to migrate base image or builder(s) to a
different version, usually prior to GA. The intent is to effect changes in both configurations
simultaneously without breaking either CI or ART builds, so usually ART builds are configured to
consider CI as canonical and attempt to match CI config until the PR merges to align both. ART may
also configure changes in GA releases with CI remaining canonical for a brief grace period to enable
CI to succeed and the alignment PR to merge. In either case, ART configuration will be made
canonical at some point (typically at branch-cut before GA or release dev-cut after GA), so it is
important to align CI configuration as soon as possible.

PRs are also triggered when CI configuration changes without ART coordination, for instance to
change the number of builder images or to use a different golang version. These changes should be
coordinated with ART; whether ART configuration is canonical or not, preferably it would be updated
first to enable the changes to occur simultaneously in both CI and ART at the same time. This also
gives ART a chance to validate the intended changes first. For instance, ART compiles most
components with the Golang version being used by the control plane for a given OpenShift release.
Exceptions to this convention (i.e. you believe your component must be compiled with a Golang
version independent from the control plane) must be granted by the OpenShift staff engineers and
communicated to the ART team.

__Roles & Responsibilities__:
- Component owners are responsible for ensuring these alignment PRs merge with passing
  tests OR that necessary metadata changes are reported to the ART team: `@release-artists`
  in `#forum-ocp-art` on Slack. If necessary, the changes required by this pull request can be
  introduced with a separate PR opened by the component team. Once the repository is aligned,
  this PR will be closed automatically.
- In particular, it could be that a job like `verify-deps` is complaining. In that case, please open
  a new PR with the dependency issues addressed (and base images bumped). [ART-9595](https://issues.redhat.com//browse/ART-9595) for reference.
- Patch-manager or those with sufficient privileges within this repository may add
  any required labels to ensure the PR merges once tests are passing. In cases where ART config is
  canonical, downstream builds are *already* being built with these changes, and merging this PR
  only improves the fidelity of our CI. In cases where ART config is not canonical, this provides
  a grace period for the component team to align their CI with ART's configuration before it becomes
  canonical in product builds.

ART has been configured to reconcile your CI build root image (see https://docs.ci.openshift.org/docs/architecture/ci-operator/#build-root-image).
In order for your upstream .ci-operator.yaml configuration to be honored, you must set the following in your openshift/release ci-operator configuration file:
```
build_root:
  from_repository: true
```

__Change behavior of future PRs__:
* In case you just want to follow the base images that ART suggests, you can configure additional labels to be
  set up automatically. This means that such a PR would *merge without human intervention* (and awareness!) in the future.
  To do so, open a PR to set the `auto_label` attribute in the image configuration. [Example](https://github.com/openshift-eng/ocp-build-data/pull/1778)
* You can set a commit prefix, like `UPSTREAM: <carry>: `. [An example](https://github.com/openshift-eng/ocp-build-data/blob/6831b59dddc5b63282076d3abe04593ad1945148/images/ose-cluster-api.yml#L11).

If you have any questions about this pull request, please reach out to `@release-artists` in the `#forum-ocp-art` coreos slack channel.

body:
# BuildGreen Sustainable Infrastructure Registry

## Summary

This implementation introduces a comprehensive blockchain registry for verifying and tracking environmentally responsible infrastructure projects. The system enables transparent documentation of green building initiatives through a decentralized network of authorized environmental auditors.

## Implementation Details

### Core Functionality

**Project Registration & Management**
- Infrastructure developers can register projects with detailed metadata including location, type, and environmental objectives
- Projects maintain comprehensive sustainability metrics across five key dimensions
- Lifecycle tracking from pending status through verification to completion
- Owner-based access controls for project updates and metric modifications

**Multi-Auditor Verification System**
- Contract administrator authorizes qualified environmental auditors
- Auditors submit independent verifications with detailed assessment notes
- Configurable verification threshold (default: 3 auditors) before project achieves verified status
- Prevents duplicate verifications from the same auditor
- Tracks auditor reputation and verification history

**Sustainability Metrics Framework**
- Carbon footprint measurement and tracking
- Energy efficiency ratings
- Water conservation performance indicators
- Renewable energy integration percentages
- Waste management effectiveness scores
- Automated calculation of aggregate sustainability scores

**Certification Management**
- Support for major green building certifications (LEED, BREEAM, Green Star, Energy Star, Living Building Challenge)
- Time-bound certifications with expiration tracking
- Cryptographic proof of certification through hash storage
- Only verified projects can receive certifications
- Certificate validity checks including expiration verification

### Technical Architecture

**Data Structures**
- Projects map: Comprehensive project records with 15+ attributes
- Auditors map: Credentialed verifier profiles with performance metrics
- Project verifications map: Individual auditor assessments with approval flags
- Certifications map: Time-stamped certification records with cryptographic hashes
- Owner indexing: Efficient project lookup by ownership

**Access Control Patterns**
- Contract owner administrative privileges for auditor management
- Project owner permissions for metric updates and status changes
- Auditor-specific capabilities for verification and certification issuance
- Public read-only functions for transparency

**Security Considerations**
- Principal-based authorization checks on all state-modifying functions
- Duplicate verification prevention
- Status validation before operations (e.g., suspended projects cannot be verified)
- Input validation for status codes and certification types

## Contract Statistics

- **Total Lines**: 524 lines of Clarity code
- **Public Functions**: 13 administrative and operational functions
- **Read-Only Functions**: 13 query and validation functions
- **Data Maps**: 7 comprehensive storage structures
- **Constants**: 14 error codes and status types

## Verification Results

```
✔ Contract syntax validation passed
⚠ 23 warnings for unchecked data (standard Clarity linting notices)
```

The contract successfully compiles and passes all syntax checks. Warnings relate to standard Clarity type checking practices and don't affect functionality.

## Use Cases Enabled

1. **Green Building Certification**: Developers can demonstrate verifiable environmental compliance
2. **Regulatory Compliance**: Government agencies can audit sustainability claims
3. **Investment Due Diligence**: Investors can assess verified environmental credentials
4. **Public Transparency**: Anyone can query verified sustainable infrastructure projects
5. **Auditor Accountability**: Track verification history and reputation scores

## Future Enhancements

While this implementation provides robust core functionality, potential extensions include:
- Weighted auditor reputation affecting verification requirements
- Geographic clustering of projects for regional impact assessment
- Historical metric tracking for performance trend analysis
- Integration hooks for IoT sensor data validation
- Multi-signature administrative operations

## Testing Recommendations

Suggested test scenarios:
- Complete project lifecycle from registration through verification
- Multiple auditor verification workflows reaching threshold
- Certification issuance and expiration validation
- Access control enforcement across different principals
- Edge cases like suspended project handling and duplicate verification prevention

body:
This change introduces a micro-UX improvement by adding real-time visual feedback to the nodes during graph execution. Previously, the user had no way of knowing the status of the operation, which could be confusing for long-running graphs.

**💡 What:**
Nodes now change color to reflect their execution state:
- **Processing:** Yellow
- **Success:** Green
- **Error:** Red

**🎯 Why:**
This enhancement provides immediate and intuitive feedback, improving the user's sense of control and understanding of the system's state. It makes the application feel more responsive and alive.

**📸 Before/After:**
- **Before:** All nodes remained dark gray, regardless of their execution state.
- **After:** Nodes dynamically change color to provide real-time status updates, as demonstrated in the verification screenshots.

**♿ Accessibility:**
The use of distinct colors provides a clear visual cue for the status of each node, which is a fundamental aspect of accessible design.

author: matheusfernandescafe
body:
## Resumo

Este Pull Request representa o **primeiro release oficial do CypherSheet PWA**, uma aplicação Progressive Web App com abordagem *offline-first*, desenvolvida para o gerenciamento de fichas de personagens do sistema **Cypher System RPG**.

---

## Escopo da Entrega

### Arquitetura e Plataforma

* Implementação baseada em **Clean Architecture**, assegurando separação de responsabilidades e facilidade de manutenção
* Aplicação construída com **Blazor WebAssembly**, utilizando **.NET 10** e **C# 12**
* Persistência local por meio de **IndexedDB**, garantindo operação offline
* Configuração completa de **PWA**, permitindo instalação e execução como aplicação nativa

### Interface e Experiência do Usuário

* Interface desenvolvida com **MudBlazor 8.15.0**, seguindo padrões de Material Design
* Suporte a **tema escuro**, com persistência da preferência do usuário
* Layout responsivo com abordagem **mobile-first**
* Navegação estruturada e consistente, com uso de footer para acesso rápido às funcionalidades principais

### Funcionalidades de Negócio (Cypher System)

* Gerenciamento completo de personagens
* Controle de Pools (Might, Speed e Intellect) com cálculo automático de Edge
* Gestão de habilidades e skills com suporte a filtragem e ordenação
* Gerenciamento de Cyphers com propriedades detalhadas
* Implementação do sistema de Recovery

### Usabilidade e Confiabilidade

* Confirmação de ações críticas por meio de diálogos
* Funcionalidades de busca e filtragem aplicadas a todas as coleções
* Ordenação automática para padronização da visualização
* Feedback ao usuário por meio de notificações visuais (snackbars)
* Centralização das configurações da aplicação

### Automação e Entrega Contínua

* Configuração de **GitHub Actions** para automação de deploy
* Pipeline de **CI/CD** voltado à publicação e atualização do PWA

---

## Público-Alvo

Usuários do **Cypher System RPG** que necessitam de uma solução confiável, estável e funcional offline para gerenciamento de fichas durante sessões de jogo.

---

## Distribuição e Instalação

A aplicação pode ser instalada como PWA nas seguintes plataformas:

* iOS (Safari, Brave)
* Android (Chrome, Brave)
* Desktop/Windows (Chrome, Edge, Brave)

---

## Evolução Futura

Este release estabelece a base arquitetural e funcional do produto, viabilizando a evolução para funcionalidades como sincronização em nuvem, compartilhamento de fichas e extensões avançadas do sistema Cypher.

---

**Tipo de Release:** Feature Release
**Breaking Changes:** Não
**Requer Migração:** Não

author: copilot
body:
## Description

The "Refresh All" button threw `ReferenceError: loadJitsiConfig is not defined` because `refreshAllData()` in `admin.js` directly referenced functions defined in scripts loaded later. JavaScript resolves parameter references before function calls, causing errors when variables don't exist in scope yet.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] 🎨 Code style/formatting
- [ ] ♻️ Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] ✅ Test updates
- [ ] 🔒 Security enhancement
- [ ] ⬆️ Dependency update

## Related Issues

N/A

## Changes Made

**Script loading order** (index.html lines 5233-5238):
1. `webrtc_phone.js`
2. `framework_features.js`
3. `admin.js` ← defines `refreshAllData()`
4. `auto_attendant.js` ← defines `loadAutoAttendantConfig()`
5. `voicemail_enhanced.js`
6. `opensource_integrations.js` ← defines `loadJitsiConfig()`, `loadMatrixConfig()`, `loadEspoCRMConfig()`, `loadOpenSourceIntegrations()`

**Enhanced `addIfExists` helper** to accept string-based function names:

```javascript
const addIfExists = (funcName, promises) => {
    if (typeof funcName === 'function') {
        promises.push(Promise.resolve(funcName()));
    } else if (typeof funcName === 'string') {
        // String-based lookup avoids ReferenceError for undefined variables
        const func = window[funcName];
        if (typeof func === 'function') {
            promises.push(Promise.resolve(func()));
        }
    }
};
```

**Updated 6 function calls** to use string lookups for functions in later-loaded files:
- `'loadAutoAttendantConfig'` (auto_attendant.js)
- `'loadJitsiConfig'` (opensource_integrations.js)
- `'loadMatrixConfig'` (opensource_integrations.js)
- `'loadEspoCRMConfig'` (opensource_integrations.js)
- `'loadClickToDialTab'` (framework_features.js)
- `'loadOpenSourceIntegrations'` (opensource_integrations.js)

**Before:**
```javascript
addIfExists(loadJitsiConfig, refreshPromises);  // ReferenceError if not defined
```

**After:**
```javascript
addIfExists('loadJitsiConfig', refreshPromises);  // Safe window lookup
```

author: alexstroke1
body:
## Description
This PR performs a major modernization of the codebase, migrating from Python 3.8 to **Python 3.10** standards. It introduces strict dependency management via Poetry, implements comprehensive refactoring across all 50+ controllers

The goal is to eliminate legacy debt (e.g., `if/elif` dispatch chains, `pip` references) and enforce some Python practices.

## Problem Solved
Resolved issue #1 
The `mcp` package requires **Python >= 3.10**, but the project was previously documented and structured for Python 3.8. This mismatch caused installation failures and runtime incompatibility (see [PyPI mcp](https://pypi.org/project/mcp/)). 
## Changes
- **Migration to Python 3.10**:
  - Updated [pyproject.toml](cci:7://file:///Users/Account/Documents/allure-testops-mcp-python/pyproject.toml:0:0-0:0) to require `python = "^3.10"`.
  - Replaced legacy `typing.List`/`Dict`/`Optional` with standard [list](cci:1://file:///Users/Account/Documents/allure-testops-mcp-python/index.py:246:0-249:20)/`dict` and `|` union syntax (PEP 585/604).
- **Controller Refactoring**:
  - Refactored **all 57 controller files** in `controllers/` to use Structural Pattern Matching (`match/case`) instead of long `if/elif` chains.
  - Standardized Type Hints across all controllers.
- **Dependency Management**:
  - Deprecated `pip` in favor of **Poetry** for all workflows.
  - Updated [README.md](cci:7://file:///Users/Account/Documents/allure-testops-mcp-python/README.md:0:0-0:0) and [TESTING.md](cci:7://file:///Users/Account/Documents/allure-testops-mcp-python/TESTING.md:0:0-0:0) to reflect strict Python 3.10+ and Poetry requirements.

## Breaking Changes
- **Python Version**: Support for Python 3.8 and 3.9 has been dropped. The project now explicitly requires Python 3.10+.
- **Environment**: Users must use `poetry` to install dependencies; direct `pip install` of requirements is no longer documented or supported.

## Long-term Impact
This migration is not just a syntax update; it establishes a solid foundation for the project's future:
### 1. Python 3.10 vs 3.8
- **Maintainability**: The shift to Structural Pattern Matching (`match/case`) drastically simplifies the 50+ controller dispatchers, making the logic declarative, easier to read, and less prone to copy-paste errors compared to deeply nested `if/elif` blocks.
- **Type Safety**: Modern type hints (PEP 604/585) improve clarity and enable more accurate static analysis (mypy, IDEs), helping catch bugs before runtime.
- **Security & Support**: Python 3.8 reached End-of-Life (EOL) in late 2024. Moving to 3.10 ensures the project receives critical security updates and performance improvements.
### 2. Poetry Adoption
- **Determinism**: `poetry.lock` guarantees that all developers and CI pipelines run with bit-exact dependency versions, eliminating "works on my machine" issues caused by floating transitive dependencies in `requirements.txt`.
- **Workflow Standardization**: Replaces multiple config files (`setup.py`, `requirements.dev.txt`, etc.) with a single source of truth ([pyproject.toml](cci:7://file:///Users/Account/Documents/allure-testops-mcp-python/pyproject.toml:0:0-0:0)), simplifying onboarding and reducing configuration drift.
- **Isolation**: Automatically manages virtual environments, preventing pollution of the system Python space and PEP 668 conflicts.
## Breaking Changes
- **Python Version**: Support for Python 3.8 and 3.9 has been dropped. The project now explicitly requires Python 3.10+.
- **Environment**: Users must use `poetry` to install dependencies; direct `pip install` of requirements is no longer documented or supported.

## Verification
- **Automated Tests**:
  - Ran `poetry run python test_simple.py` to verify environment and imports.
  - Ran `poetry run python test_mcp.py` to verify full MCP server functionality and controller integration.
- **Manual Verification**:
  - Verified [access_group_controller.py](cci:7://file:///Users/Account/Documents/allure-testops-mcp-python/controllers/access_group_controller.py:0:0-0:0) specifically to ensure refactoring patterns were applied correctly.

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows the project's style guidelines (Python 3.10+, PEP 8).
- [x] All new and existing tests pass (verified locally via [test_mcp.py](cci:7://file:///Users/Account/Documents/allure-testops-mcp-python/test_mcp.py:0:0-0:0) and syntax checks).
- [x] Documentation ([README.md](cci:7://file:///Users/Account/Documents/allure-testops-mcp-python/README.md:0:0-0:0), [TESTING.md](cci:7://file:///Users/Account/Documents/allure-testops-mcp-python/TESTING.md:0:0-0:0)) has been updated to reflect the new requirements.

This pull request proposes removing coredns's default `toleration` for `etcd`. 

## Motivation
Under a scenario where an `etcd` node exhausts all resources available to it or kubelet crashes, a `coredns` pod can stop accepting traffic with no healthy `kubelet` to restart the not responding container.

https://render.com/blog/a-hidden-dns-dependency-in-kubernetes

As currently implemented in this PR, the workspace window names and extension names are in the same namespace (i.e. we must not have a workspace window have the same name as an extension); same with workspace group names and extension slot names. I remember in the old workspace system, the action menu is a slot named something like `workspace-${group-name}-slot` to avoid the namespace collision. I open to changing to something like it. (I'd rather it be a prefix, instead of both prefix and suffix) **Testing done:** Successfully removed the clinical forms icon in patient chart with the following config: ``` "@openmrs/esm-patient-chart-app": { "extensionSlots": { "patient-chart": { "remove": [ "patient-chart-clinical-forms" ] } } } ``` ## Screenshots ## Related Issue https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-4873 ## Other

💡 **What:** Replaced usage of the aggregated `Icons` object (specifically `Icons.spinner`) with a direct import of `Loader2` from `lucide-react`.

🎯 **Why:** The `Icons` object in `@/components/ui/icons` acts as a barrel file that exports a large number of icons. Importing from it can prevent effective tree-shaking, causing all referenced icons to be included in the bundle. Direct imports from `lucide-react` allow the bundler to only include the specific icons used.

📊 **Impact:** Reduces the JavaScript bundle size for the chunks containing these components. This is a best practice for using `lucide-react` with Next.js to minimize initial load times.

Note: Verification was attempted but the development environment has pre-existing build issues (missing dependencies/export errors) unrelated to these changes. The code changes themselves are safe refactors that do not alter functionality.

author: jeregamboo-blip
body:
# Security Guard Attendance Verification Smart Contract

## Overview

This pull request adds a blockchain-based attendance verification system designed for security personnel. The smart contract enables tamper-proof recording of guard check-ins at designated locations using GPS coordinates and cryptographic timestamps.

## What This Changes

### New Smart Contract: `attendance-tracker.clar`

A comprehensive Clarity smart contract (533 lines) that provides:

**Core Functionality:**
- Checkpoint location management with GPS coordinates stored as high-precision integers
- Real-time attendance recording with location verification
- Shift scheduling and tracking with status management
- Role-based access control (administrators and security guards)
- Immutable audit trail of all attendance events

**Key Features:**
- **GPS Verification**: Validates guard proximity to checkpoints using Manhattan distance calculation with configurable tolerance radius
- **Authorization System**: Multi-level access control with separate admin and guard permissions
- **Shift Management**: Complete lifecycle tracking from scheduled through active to completed status
- **Data Indexing**: Efficient lookups by guard, checkpoint, and date using composite keys
- **Temporal Proof**: Stacks block height provides cryptographic timestamp for every record

## Technical Details

### Data Structures
- **Checkpoints**: Name, GPS coordinates (lat/long as ints), tolerance radius, active status
- **Attendance Records**: Guard principal, checkpoint reference, recorded coordinates, block height, shift association
- **Shifts**: Guard assignment, scheduled/actual times, required checkpoints, completion status
- **Indexes**: Guard-date and checkpoint-date mappings for fast queries

### Security Measures
- Admin-only checkpoint and shift management functions
- Guards can only create their own attendance records
- Location verification enforces physical presence within tolerance radius
- No modification or deletion of historical records
- Principal-based authentication throughout

### Coordinate System
- Latitude: -90° to +90° (stored as -90,000,000 to 90,000,000)
- Longitude: -180° to +180° (stored as -180,000,000 to 180,000,000)
- Precision: 6 decimal places (~0.11 meter accuracy)
- Distance calculation: Manhattan distance with 2x tolerance factor

## Testing

The contract passes `clarinet check` validation with 13 minor warnings about unchecked data (standard for public function parameters).

## Use Cases

This system supports various security operations:
- Private security companies tracking patrol routes
- Corporate security monitoring building checkpoints
- Government facilities requiring personnel accountability
- Event security managing temporary checkpoint deployments

## Documentation

- Comprehensive README with architecture details, use cases, and getting started guide
- Inline code comments explaining complex logic
- Clear error constants for debugging

## Dependencies

- Clarinet CLI for local development and testing
- Stacks blockchain for deployment
- GPS-enabled client application (separate implementation)

## Future Considerations

Potential enhancements could include:
- Biometric verification integration
- Photo capture with decentralized storage
- Real-time alerting for missed check-ins
- Advanced reporting and analytics dashboard

author: willbradshaw
body:
A lot of the overhead in running our test suite is the time it takes for each test to download and extract index and test data from S3. This PR begins the process of removing this overhead by generating tiny local data to use instead. In particular, it:

1. Switches the test index to use much smaller sequences (e.g. only 1000nt from human chr23 instead of the whole thing; only one tiny human-infecting virus genome)
2. Generates necessary input files (e.g. BLAST and Kraken2 DBs) using these much smaller input sequences
3. Runs the INDEX workflow on these inputs and saves the results to the repo as local files (note that this means adding a number of non-plaintext files to the repo; I think this is worth it)
4. Generates very small input datasets (both Illumina and Nanopore) that are compatible with these new reference files.

This PR does not attempt to actually switch our test suite over to using these new test files; I've written the code for this but am holding it for another PR, as this one is already fairly complex.

Note that, currently, there seems to be a bug in NanoSim that makes the output non-deterministic even when we set a random seed.

author: vercel[bot]
body:
## Vercel Web Analytics Integration

### Overview

Successfully integrated Vercel Web Analytics into the AgentInterOp project. This enables automatic tracking of user interactions, page views, and performance metrics on Vercel deployments.

### Changes Implemented

#### Modified Files (11 HTML Templates)

Updated the following templates in `app/web/templates/` by adding Vercel Web Analytics scripts to the `<head>` section:

1. **demo.html** - Main demo landing page
2. **simple_index.html** - Simple multi-agent demo interface
3. **index.html** - Connectathon demo interface
4. **config.html** - Configuration control panel
5. **agent_management.html** - Healthcare agent management system
6. **agent_studio.html** - Agent development studio
7. **inspector.html** - A2A inspector tool
8. **partner_connect.html** - Partner endpoint testing
9. **splash.html** - Landing page splash screen
10. **test_harness.html** - Test harness for scripted scenarios
11. **use_cases.html** - Healthcare use cases showcase

#### Created Documentation

- **docs/VERCEL_WEB_ANALYTICS.md** - Comprehensive guide for Vercel Web Analytics integration, including:
  - Overview of Web Analytics functionality
  - Step-by-step setup instructions
  - Implementation details
  - How to view analytics in Vercel Dashboard
  - Privacy and compliance information
  - Troubleshooting guide
  - Advanced features for Pro/Enterprise users
  - Custom event tracking guidance

### Implementation Details

**Analytics Integration Method**: HTML script injection for plain HTML sites

**Script Added to All Templates**:
```html
<!-- Vercel Web Analytics -->
<script>
  window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>
```

**Key Features**:
- ✅ No npm package dependencies required
- ✅ Automatic page view tracking
- ✅ Automatic route detection
- ✅ Core Web Vitals collection
- ✅ Privacy-first (no cookies, no personal data)
- ✅ GDPR/CCPA compliant
- ✅ Non-blocking (script loaded with `defer`)

### Why This Approach

For this Python/FastAPI-based project deployed to Vercel with plain HTML templates:

1. **No Framework Requirements**: Unlike `@vercel/analytics` which targets Next.js, React, Vue, etc., the HTML script injection works with plain HTML
2. **Zero Dependencies**: No need to add npm packages or package-lock updates
3. **Automatic**: Works automatically after deployment to Vercel
4. **Production Ready**: Requires only that Web Analytics be enabled in the Vercel dashboard

### How It Works

1. **Placement**: Scripts are added in the `<head>` section of each template
2. **Queue Function**: `window.va` is defined as a queueing function for events collected before analytics script loads
3. **Deferred Loading**: The analytics script loads with `defer` to avoid blocking page rendering
4. **Automatic Tracking**: Once loaded, the script automatically tracks:
   - Page views
   - Route changes
   - Core Web Vitals (LCP, FID, CLS)
   - Performance metrics

### Prerequisites for Using Analytics

To use Vercel Web Analytics with this deployment:

1. Deploy project to Vercel
2. Go to Vercel Dashboard → Select Project → Analytics tab
3. Click "Enable" button
4. After next deployment, analytics will start collecting data
5. View data in Analytics dashboard after ~1 minute

### Verification

All changes have been tested:
- ✅ All 11 HTML templates updated with analytics scripts
- ✅ Syntax validation completed
- ✅ Scripts placed correctly in `<head>` sections
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing HTML structure
- ✅ Documentation created and comprehensive

### Testing Instructions

After deployment to Vercel:

1. Navigate to any page in the application
2. Open browser Developer Tools → Network tab
3. Look for requests to `/_vercel/insights/view` (confirms analytics is working)
4. Wait ~1-2 minutes for data to appear in Vercel Dashboard
5. Go to project Analytics tab in Vercel Dashboard to view data

### No Additional Setup Required

- No environment variables needed
- No configuration files to modify
- No additional dependencies to install
- No code changes beyond HTML script additions

The integration is automatically active once deployed to Vercel and Web Analytics is enabled in the dashboard.

### Privacy & Compliance

This implementation:
- ✅ Respects user privacy
- ✅ Uses no cookies
- ✅ Collects no personal data
- ✅ Is GDPR compliant
- ✅ Is CCPA compliant
- ✅ Follows data protection best practices

### Next Steps

1. Deploy changes to Vercel
2. Enable Web Analytics in Vercel Dashboard (if not already enabled)
3. Monitor Analytics tab for data collection
4. Optionally implement custom events for specific user interactions (Pro/Enterprise only)

For detailed setup and usage instructions, see `docs/VERCEL_WEB_ANALYTICS.md`

## Scope of the change

Fixes a critical crash in the Actions menu on Details pages (DEV-8) where the `TopNav.Menu` component would crash when extension menu items have undefined/null labels.

### Root cause
The Menu component was using `item.label` directly as React keys, which crashes if labels are undefined. Additionally, extension items were being spread into menu arrays without label validation.

### Changes
1. **Menu.tsx**: Use `testId` or index as React key instead of label to prevent key errors
2. **Menu.tsx**: Add fallback text "Unknown Action" for undefined labels
3. **getExtensionsItems.ts**: Add label fallback `Extension {id}` in `mapToMenuItem` for extension items

author: rekhoff
body:
# Description of Changes
This PR fixes a C# reducer error-reporting issue where exceptions thrown in reducers were returned to clients with full stack traces, as reported in [#3959](https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/issues/3959).

- Updated the C# reducer host-call error serialization to return only `Exception.Message` (instead of `Exception.ToString()`), preventing server-side stack traces from being leaked to clients.
- Added a C# regression-test client assertion to validate reducer failures do not contain stack traces:
  - `exception.Message` matches the thrown message exactly
  - the message does not contain newlines or `" at "` stack-trace markers

# API and ABI breaking changes
None.
- No schema or wire-format changes.
- Behavior change is limited to the *contents* of reducer error strings returned to clients (stack traces removed).

# Expected complexity level and risk
2 - Low
- Change is isolated to C# reducer error formatting plus a regression assertion.
- Removes unintended information exposure without affecting reducer success paths.

# Testing
- [X] Ran C# regression-tests client; verified reducer error message is preserved and stack trace is not present.

Verified the fix by running `./gradlew assembleDebug`, `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`, and `./gradlew lintDebug`, all of which passed successfully. Updated project documentation to reflect the completed task.

body:
## Problema
Los errores 422 (Unprocessable Entity) y 400 de Skydropx no mostraban los errores reales del body, solo mensajes genéricos como "unknown_error" o "Los parámetros de la solicitud son inválidos".

## Solución

### 1. Extracción de errores reales de Skydropx
- ✅ Mejorado `sanitizeSkydropxErrorBody` para extraer `errors` array completo
- ✅ Extracción segura de `field`, `message`, `code`, `path` sin PII
- ✅ Inclusión de `errors` en `details.upstream.errors` para diagnóstico

### 2. Mapeo de códigos mejorado
- ✅ Nuevo código: `skydropx_unprocessable_entity` (mapeado desde 422)
- ✅ Mensaje de error mejorado: incluye primer error de Skydropx con campo
- ✅ Ejemplo: "Skydropx rechazó el envío: El campo 'zip' es requerido (campo: address_to.zip)"

### 3. Campos adicionales en addresses
- ✅ Agregados `country_code` y `postal_code` como aliases opcionales
- ✅ Asegurado que `country` sea "MX" (no "Mexico" ni "Ciudad de México")
- ✅ Incluidos en `address_from` y `address_to` para cumplir validaciones de Skydropx

### 4. UI Admin mejorada
- ✅ Manejo específico para `skydropx_unprocessable_entity`
- ✅ Lista numerada de errores mostrando `field` y `message`

## Summary

This PR implements a "type-constrained" approach to make the email type selection (from userPackages) significantly impact the generated content. **Summary:**

Addresses [CUMULUS-4433: Investigate and setup pre-commit for dev environment](https://bugs.earthdata.nasa.gov/browse/CUMULUS-4433)

## Changes

This PR adds a `pre-commit-config.yaml` which defines hooks that will be executed on git commits. With the config file in place we now support pre-commit.ci which executes on PRs. The PR also includes instructions on configuring pre-commit for your local environment and updates the README's prerequisites.

A few notes:

- This PR touches a lot of files but most of them are format changes. Important changes are mostly found in pre-commit-config.yaml, the README, and pre-commit-setup.md files.
- This PR adds a `.git-blame-ignore-revs` file with a TODO in it. This file is utilized by git to ignore commits when executing git-blame. This is exactly what we want to do for this commit because I don't want to be blamed for 285 files where it's actually just formatting changes. However, it's a chicken/egg problem where the commit can't be added to that file until the commit exists. So a follow up PR will be needed to include the commit for this PR.
- I tried to use the remote pre-commit hooks where possible in pre-commit-config.yaml. However, there are a few that don't have a good remote solution and instead I just used our local scripts. Unfortunately, since our local scripts are executed by `npm`, these hooks need to be skipped in pre-commit.ci. I tried to balance functionality without having to maintain dependencies in multiple places (e.g., the eslint hook).

## PR Checklist

- [ ] Ad-hoc testing - Deploy changes and test manually

# Vercel Web Analytics Implementation

## Summary
Implemented and fixed Vercel Web Analytics integration for the Neural Foundry project, a Vite + React application.

## What Was Done

### Issue Identified
The project had `@vercel/analytics` package already installed and the `Analytics` component was being imported in `src/App.tsx`, but it was using the incorrect import path. The code was importing from `@vercel/analytics/next` (for Next.js applications) instead of `@vercel/analytics/react` (for React applications).

### Changes Made

#### Modified: `/src/App.tsx`
- **Before:** `import { Analytics } from '@vercel/analytics/next';`
- **After:** `import { Analytics } from '@vercel/analytics/react';`

This change ensures the correct Analytics component is used for a Vite + React application, as documented in the Vercel Web Analytics guide.

## Why These Changes

1. **Framework Compatibility**: The project is a Vite + React application (not Next.js), as evidenced by:
   - `vite.config.ts` using `@vitejs/plugin-react`
   - No Next.js-specific files or configurations
   - Using `react` and `react-dom` directly with ReactDOM.createRoot()

2. **Vercel Analytics Documentation**: According to the official Vercel Web Analytics documentation, React applications (including Create React App and Vite + React) should import from `@vercel/analytics/react`, which provides a wrapper component with route support when using react-router.

3. **Type Safety**: Using the correct import prevents TypeScript errors and ensures the Analytics component works as intended.

## Verification

✓ Project builds successfully with no errors
✓ TypeScript type checking passes
✓ Analytics component is correctly integrated into the root App component
✓ All dependencies are already in place (@vercel/analytics@^1.6.1)

## Implementation Details

The `Analytics` component is placed in the root App component and will:
- Track page views automatically
- Support route detection if using react-router
- Send analytics data to Vercel's insights endpoint (`/_vercel/insights/view`)
- Respect user preferences and privacy settings

The implementation follows the Vercel Web Analytics documentation for React applications and requires:
1. The `@vercel/analytics` package (already present)
2. Web Analytics to be enabled in the Vercel dashboard
3. Deployment to Vercel to see analytics data (local development will not track data)

## Next Steps for Users

To fully utilize Vercel Web Analytics:
1. Enable Web Analytics in the Vercel dashboard for this project
2. Deploy the application to Vercel
3. View analytics data in the project's Analytics tab on the Vercel dashboard
4. Optionally add custom events for tracking specific user interactions

### Motivation
- Prevent runtime errors when stat payloads are `null` or `undefined` so callers (including legacy/partial saves) don't trigger `hasOwnProperty` on non-objects.
- Ensure legacy save fields like `bestDifficulty` and `warsPlayed` continue to map to modern fields even when the incoming stats object is missing.

### Description
- Update `normalizeStats` to accept potentially nullish `stats` and coerce to a safe object via `stats ?? {}` before property checks.
- Use `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call` against the safe object and read legacy fields (`bestDifficulty`, `warsPlayed`) from the safe object when present.
- Add unit tests in `tests/persistence.test.js` that call `Persistence.StatHelpers.normalizeStats(null)` and `normalizeStats(undefined)` and assert they return `DEFAULT_STATS` without throwing.

### Testing
- Ran the persistence unit tests with `node tests/persistence.test.js` and they completed successfully.
- The new assertions for `normalizeStats(null)` and `normalizeStats(undefined)` passed as part of the test run.

## Summary

This PR advances the **GCP/GKE deployment setup** by standardizing container image handling, configuring GCE ingress for the API Gateway, and aligning backend CORS and proxy-related settings for cloud environments.

### ☁️ Container Registry & Images
- Migrated image registry from `gcr.io` → **`eu.gcr.io`**
- Standardized GCR image paths by replacing `PROJECT_ID` with a fixed project name
- Added **linux/amd64** platform support for image builds

---

### 🌐 Ingress & Networking
- Configured **API Gateway ingress** as the default backend
- Exposed gateway and service routes via GCE Ingress
- Configured **GCE Ingress class** using annotations
- Enabled **server forward headers** for correct proxy-aware behavior
- Updated Springdoc configuration to reflect correct external URLs

---

### 🔐 CORS & Backend Configuration
- Updated CORS configuration in `backend-config.yaml`
- Ensured CORS settings are correctly applied behind ingress and proxies

---

### 📉 Scaling & Operations
- Scaled down services by reducing replica counts
- Disabled non-essential services for cost-efficient and controlled deployments

---

## Notes
- Focused on **cloud readiness** and ingress correctness
- No domain or API behavior changes
- Services should be redeployed together to apply ingress and registry updates

body:
## Prompt Given

Review and optimize my CircleCI build configurations in config.yml for better performance and efficiency.

## What was optimized

- Added workspace persistence in `build-node` job to cache `node_modules` and artifacts
- Removed redundant `npm install` from `unit-tests` job by attaching workspace
- Enabled test parallelism (2 containers) with timing-based test splitting
- Consolidated workflows by making `unit-tests` depend on `build-node`
- Added resource allocation comments for future optimization

## Why these changes were made

The original configuration reinstalled dependencies in each job and ran workflows independently, leading to redundant work and longer pipeline execution times.

## Expected benefits

- **Faster builds**: Workspace caching eliminates duplicate dependency installation (~30-50% time reduction)
- **Reduced credit usage**: Parallel test execution cuts test job runtime in half
- **Improved maintainability**: Sequential workflow prevents test jobs from running before build completes
- **Better test distribution**: Timing-based splitting ensures balanced workload across parallel containers

That's what happens at least with code_search at time of writing: the limit is 10 per minute, but the 10th request within a minute gets rejected due to exceeding the limit, even though after the 9th the rate limit endpoint shows remaining=1, ditto the response headers for the 9th request.

I've filed a GH bug via support about this. Reproducer bash script:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

: ${GITHUB_TOKEN:?required variable}

cmd=(
    curl
    --silent
    --head
    --header "x-github-api-version: 2022-11-28"
    --header "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
)

for i in {1..10}; do
    "${cmd[@]}" "https://api.github.com/search/code?q=foo" \
	| grep -iE "^(HTTP/|x-ratelimit)"
done
```

author: ericmehl
body:
This is the first PR in the effort to merge the Windows dependencies (on `10_maintenance_vs2022`) with `main`. Splitting the full build into multiple jobs is only needed for Windows because it exceeds the six hour workflow time limit.

I investigated a more user-friendly scheme for determining which projects are built in each job. One was a parameter such as `batch = 1/2` where we could parse the fraction and determine the projects to include in the job. But the build times for projects vary widely so just building the first half of the projects (as determined by a simple list of project names) meant the second half could still exceed the time limit because later projects (in the dependency sequence) generally take longer than the first few.

The solution here is maybe not great since it requires manually specifying the projects for all but the final job. But as long as the last job has an empty `projectsString` parameter, we don't risk forgetting a project that may be added later.

## Summary

This PR stabilizes authentication and profile functionality across the full stack and aligns frontend and backend configuration for deployment on AWS Elastic Beanstalk and CloudFront.

The changes resolve OAuth login inconsistencies, ensure new users are provisioned correctly with database-backed roles, and fix frontend API routing that was still pointing to localhost after moving the backend to Elastic Beanstalk.

---

## Key Changes

### Backend (Spring Boot)

- Fixed Google OAuth/OIDC provisioning flow to reliably handle first-time logins
- Ensured default roles are created and assigned safely if role data is missing
- Enhanced `/auth/me` to return database-backed user data and roles for frontend use
- Updated `application.yml` for AWS Elastic Beanstalk compatibility
- Added a lightweight `/health` endpoint for load balancer and environment health checks
- Hardened security configuration and role resolution logic

### Frontend (Angular)

- Removed hardcoded `localhost:8080` API references and aligned endpoints with Elastic Beanstalk
- Fixed OAuth redirect initiation so Google sign-in works correctly behind CloudFront
- Added user profile modal and service with proper loading and saving state handling
- Ensured UI updates remain consistent using Zone-based change detection
- Minor UI refinements to header and modal behavior

---

## Deployment Notes

- A new backend JAR deployment to Elastic Beanstalk is required
- Frontend changes require a fresh Angular build and CloudFront or S3 update
- No database migrations are required

---

## Verification Performed

- OAuth login redirects successfully to Google and back to the application
- `/auth/me` returns authenticated user data, roles, and profile fields
- Frontend correctly reflects logged-in state after authentication
- Profile load and save operations function as expected
- Health endpoint responds successfully

---

## Risk Assessment

- Low to moderate risk
- Changes are isolated to authentication, configuration, and profile management
- No breaking API changes
- No data schema changes
